The question, asked formally and with authority, gave Peter a public platform he did not seek but would now use. God often turns hostile interrogation into opportunity for testimony.
4:7.reflection: When hard questions come my way about my faith, do I see them as threats or as openings to speak of Jesus?
4:7.action: Prepare for hard questions by reviewing briefly why you believe Jesus is trustworthy, so you can answer with calm confidence.
4:7.prayer: Lord, You turned a courtroom interrogation into an opportunity for testimony. Help me see challenging questions about my faith not as dangers but as doors. Fill my mouth with gracious, truthful words when the moment comes. Amen.

4:8.devotion: Peter answered the council filled with the Holy Spirit, just as Jesus had promised His followers would be when brought before authorities. The fisherman who once denied Jesus around a fire now stood composed before the high priestly court. This verse is a picture of God equipping His servants in the very moment of need.
4:8.reflection: Where am I relying on my own ability to speak for Christ instead of asking the Spirit's help?
4:8.action: Before any conversation today where you feel nervous, pause and silently ask the Holy Spirit for wisdom and calm words.
4:8.prayer: Holy Spirit, You filled Peter for the moment of testing, and You are present with me now. Fill me afresh today. Make me bold where I am timid and clear where I am confused, for Jesus' sake. Amen.

4:9.devotion: Peter opened his defense by pointing to the absurdity of the situation: they were on trial for a kindness done to a helpless man. Healing a man who had begged at the temple gate for years was not a crime. Peter respectfully reframed the hearing, inviting the council to consider the obvious goodness of what had occurred.
4:9.reflection: Am I willing to let good works done in Christ's name speak for themselves when my faith is questioned?
4:9.action: Do one quiet act of kindness for someone in need today, without seeking credit, and let the deed witness on its own.
4:9.prayer: Father, You delight in mercy shown to those in need. Keep my hands busy with good works that honor You, and give me humility to serve without applause. May kindness done in Jesus' name open doors for His story. Amen.

4:10.devotion: Peter stands before the Sanhedrin after healing a lame man, boldly naming the power behind it: Jesus Christ of Nazareth. He confronts their role in His crucifixion while declaring God's triumph in raising Him. The healing is presented as evidence that the crucified and risen Jesus is still at work.
4:10.reflection: Where in my life am I relying on my own strength instead of the name and power of the risen Jesus?
4:10.action: Today, when a need or challenge arises, pause and specifically ask God to work through Jesus' name rather than rushing ahead on your own.
4:10.prayer: Lord Jesus, You were rejected by men but raised by God. Work in the places where I am weak and broken, and let my life point others to Your power. Amen.

4:11.devotion: Quoting Psalm 118, Peter applies to Jesus the image of a stone the builders rejected that became the cornerstone. The religious leaders, the supposed builders of Israel's life, had discarded Jesus, yet God made Him the essential foundation of His saving work.
4:11.reflection: Is Jesus truly the cornerstone of my life, or have I treated Him as optional in some corner of it?
4:11.action: Identify one area of daily life—finances, work, relationships—where you have sidelined Jesus, and take one step to place His teaching at its foundation today.
4:11.prayer: Father, thank You for making Jesus the cornerstone. Forgive me for the times I have overlooked Him. Help me build my life on Him alone. Amen.

4:12.devotion: Peter stood before Israel's religious leaders, unafraid. He declared that rescue from sin comes through one person only—Jesus Christ. This isn't narrowness but God's gracious provision: heaven has supplied a single, sufficient name. No prophet, philosophy, or self-effort can save. Everyone, everywhere, meets God's offer of life at the same crossroads: trusting Christ alone.
4:12.reflection: Where am I tempted to look for hope or rescue apart from Jesus?
4:12.action: Name one person who doesn't follow Christ, and pray today for a natural opening this week to share how Jesus saved you.
4:12.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for being the only name that saves. Forgive me for times I've trusted lesser things. Give me courage like Peter's to confess You plainly, and lead someone today toward Your saving grace. Amen.

4:13.devotion: The council notices that Peter and John, ordinary men without formal rabbinic training, speak with remarkable courage. Their boldness and clarity point to one explanation: they had been with Jesus. Time spent with Christ marked their speech and character in a way others could recognize.
4:13.reflection: Would the people around me be able to tell from my words and courage that I have been with Jesus?
4:13.action: Spend unhurried time with Jesus today in Scripture and prayer, and let one conversation reflect His grace and confidence.
4:13.prayer: Jesus, make me recognizable as Yours. Shape my words, courage, and character through time spent with You, so that others may glimpse You in me. Amen.

4:14.devotion: The healed man stands beside Peter and John, a living witness no one can argue with. The council wants to silence the apostles, but the evident transformation of a real person leaves them without a response. Changed lives testify powerfully to the gospel.
4:14.reflection: How has God's work in my life become a quiet testimony that others can see, not just words I say?
4:14.action: Share with one person today a specific way God has changed or sustained you, giving Him the credit plainly and humbly.
4:14.prayer: Father, thank You for the work You have done in me. Make my life a honest witness to Your grace, and use my story to point others to Jesus. Amen.

4:15.devotion: Unable to refute the miracle, the council removes Peter and John from the room to confer privately. Their deliberation shows hearts more committed to protecting their authority than to discovering the truth standing before them. Opposition often begins with private scheming rather than open examination.
4:15.reflection: Am I willing to examine evidence honestly when God's work challenges my assumptions or comforts?
4:15.action: When you feel defensive about a belief or decision today, pause and honestly ask God to show you the truth before you respond.
4:15.prayer: Lord, give me an honest heart that seeks Your truth rather than defending my own position. Protect me from pride that refuses to see Your work. Amen.

4:16.devotion: Even the council's members admit among themselves that the miracle is undeniable and known throughout Jerusalem. The issue is not lack of evidence but unwillingness to accept its implications. They acknowledge God's evident work while still plotting to suppress its message.
4:16.reflection: Is there evidence of God's work that I acknowledge but resist acting on because it would demand change from me?
4:16.action: Name one truth about God you have known but resisted obeying, and take a first concrete step of obedience today.
4:16.prayer: Father, forgive me for the times I have seen Your work yet hesitated to respond. Give me the courage to follow truth wherever it leads. Amen.

4:17.devotion: Rather than responding to the miracle, the council decides to manage the situation through intimidation, planning severe threats to stop the apostles from speaking about Jesus. It is a strategy of silence: suppress the message rather than grapple with the reality behind it.
4:17.reflection: When confronted with truth that unsettles me, do I seek God or try to manage and quiet the situation?
4:17.action: Notice one moment today when you are tempted to avoid or hush a spiritual matter, and instead bring it honestly to God in prayer.
4:17.prayer: Lord, keep me from silencing Your truth to protect my comfort. Give me wisdom to face what You reveal and boldness never to be ashamed of Jesus. Amen.

4:18.devotion: The council formally commands Peter and John not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus. Authority is wielded to shut down testimony about the risen Christ. Yet this official prohibition sets the stage for the apostles' famous answer that they must obey God rather than men.
4:18.reflection: Under what pressures—social, professional, or relational—am I tempted to stay quiet about Jesus?
4:18.action: Choose one natural, appropriate opportunity today to mention your faith in Jesus respectfully, despite any awkwardness you feel.
4:18.prayer: Father, You are greater than every authority that resists You. When I feel pressured to be silent about Jesus, give me gracious courage to speak and live for Him. Amen.

4:19.devotion: Peter and John had been arrested for healing a lame man and preaching Jesus. Facing the council's orders to keep silent, they respectfully but firmly placed God's authority above human commands. Their question reminds us that when authorities contradict God, our first allegiance belongs to Him.
4:19.reflection: When human pressure conflicts with God's calling, whose voice do I obey?
4:19.action: Identify one area today where pleasing people tempts you to compromise obedience to God, and choose faithfulness there.
4:19.prayer: Lord, strengthen my courage to honor You above every other voice. When obedience to You costs me something, help me stand with gentleness and truth, trusting You with the results. In Jesus' name, Amen.

4:20.devotion: Peter and John explained why they could not obey the ban on preaching: they had personally witnessed the risen Christ's work. Their testimony was not secondhand opinion but lived experience. Authentic encounters with Jesus create a holy compulsion to share what we know to be true.
4:20.reflection: What has God done in my life that I find hard to keep quiet about?
4:20.action: Share one specific way God has worked in your life with a friend or family member today.
4:20.prayer: Father, thank You for the real things You have shown me of Your grace. Give me natural, honest words to share what I have seen and heard of Your goodness with those around me. Amen.

4:21.devotion: The council threatened the apostles again but released them, fearing public backlash. The healed man's restoration was undeniable, and the whole community was glorifying God for it. God's work carried its own witness, and even hostile authorities found no grounds to act against the apostles.
4:21.reflection: Do I give God public credit for the good things He does in and around me?
4:21.action: When someone compliments something good in your life today, point to God's kindness in a brief, sincere word.
4:21.prayer: Gracious God, You are at work in ways people can see. Let my life and my words glorify You openly, so that others notice Your goodness and join in praising Your name. Amen.

4:22.devotion: Luke notes the healed man was over forty years old, meaning he had lived decades with his condition. This detail underscores how remarkable and verifiable the miracle was; everyone in Jerusalem knew him. God's restorative power reached a life long marked by limitation, confirming the apostles' message about Jesus.
4:22.reflection: Where might I assume it is too late for God to bring change?
4:22.action: Bring one long-standing situation you have nearly given up on before God in honest, expectant prayer today.
4:22.prayer: Lord, nothing in my life is beyond Your reach, however long it has persisted. Help me trust Your wisdom and timing, and to hope in Your power without demanding that You act on my schedule. Amen.

4:23.devotion: Released from custody, Peter and John went straight to their fellow believers and reported everything the leaders had said. They did not isolate themselves under pressure; they brought their story into the community. Shared trials, honestly told, knit believers together and prepare the church to pray with understanding.
4:23.reflection: When I face pressure or opposition, do I carry it alone or bring it to trusted believers?
4:23.action: Tell one trusted Christian friend about a difficulty you are facing and invite them to pray with you.
4:23.prayer: Father, thank You for the gift of Christian community. Keep me from isolation when life is hard, and teach me to share burdens honestly with brothers and sisters who will pray alongside me. Amen.

4:24.devotion: Hearing the apostles' report, the church prayed together with one voice. They began not with requests but with praise, acknowledging God as Creator of heaven, earth, sea, and everything in them. Remembering who God is rightly frames every prayer, especially prayers offered under pressure and threat.
4:24.reflection: Do my prayers usually begin with my problems or with who God is?
4:24.action: Begin your next prayer today by naming God as Creator and Lord before presenting any requests.
4:24.prayer: Sovereign Lord, Maker of heaven and earth and all they contain, I lift my voice to You. Before I ask for anything, I praise You for Your greatness, faithfulness, and unfailing care. Amen.

4:25.devotion: In their united prayer, the believers recognized God's sovereign voice speaking through Scripture, quoting David's psalm. They saw their own situation connected to God's long-revealed plan. Praying Scripture anchored their courage, reminding them that the opposition they faced had been anticipated by God's Word long before.
4:25.reflection: How could praying Scripture reshape the way I face my current fears?
4:25.action: Choose one psalm or passage today and pray through its words slowly, making them your own prayer.
4:25.prayer: Father, thank You that Your Word speaks across generations into my life today. Teach me to pray Your promises back to You, finding steadiness and courage in what You have already spoken. Amen.

4:26.devotion: Continuing David's words, the church acknowledged that rulers opposing God's Messiah was no surprise; Scripture had foretold it. Rather than panic at the council's hostility, they interpreted events through God's revealed plan. Opposition to Christ does not derail God's purposes, and believers can pray with confidence in His reign.
4:26.reflection: How does remembering that God reigns change the way I view opposition or criticism?
4:26.action: Name one fear about opposition or disapproval today, and consciously entrust it to God's sovereign care in prayer.
4:26.prayer: Lord, You reign above every ruler and authority. When I face resistance for following Christ, keep me calm and courageous, trusting that Your purposes stand and nothing can overturn Your plan. Amen.

4:27.devotion: After Peter and John were released from the council, the believers prayed together. They acknowledged that Herod, Pilate, the Gentiles, and Israel's leaders had all conspired against Jesus, God's anointed Servant. Naming the opposition honestly became the beginning of a prayer that entrusted everything to God.
4:27.reflection: When I face opposition for my faith, do I bring it honestly to God rather than pretending it away?
4:27.action: Name one situation where following Jesus feels difficult, and honestly tell God about it in prayer today.
4:27.prayer: Father, You see every force that stands against Your Son and against Your people. Help me not to hide my fears from You, but to bring them honestly into Your presence and trust You with them. In Jesus' name, Amen.

4:28.devotion: Continuing their prayer, the believers declared that those who conspired against Jesus only did what God's hand and purpose had determined beforehand. Human rebellion did not derail God's plan; mysteriously, God worked through it to accomplish the salvation He had purposed.
4:28.reflection: Can I trust that God's purposes are larger and stronger than the opposition I witness or experience?
4:28.action: Write down one situation that feels out of control, and consciously entrust it to God's wise purposes today.
4:28.prayer: Lord, Your purposes stand firm even when people resist You. Thank You that nothing can frustrate Your plan. Teach me to rest in Your wisdom when circumstances confuse me, and to hope in the Savior You promised. Amen.

4:29.devotion: Facing real threats from the authorities, the believers did not ask for safety or revenge. Instead, they prayed for boldness to keep speaking God's word. Their request turned attention from the danger around them to the mission before them.
4:29.reflection: When sharing my faith feels risky or uncomfortable, what do I tend to ask God for instead of boldness?
4:29.action: Ask God for courage to speak about Him in one specific conversation or relationship this week.
4:29.prayer: Sovereign Lord, You know the pressures and threats Your people face. Like the early church, I ask not for ease but for boldness to speak Your word faithfully and graciously. Strengthen my timid heart today. In Jesus' name, Amen.

4:30.devotion: The believers asked God to stretch out His hand in healing and to work signs and wonders through the name of Jesus. Their boldness in speech was joined to a dependence on God's power, so that the message of Christ would be confirmed and hearts would be drawn to Him.
4:30.reflection: Do I pray as though God still works powerfully, or only as though everything depends on my own effort?
4:30.action: Pray today for God to work in one situation where someone needs healing, hope, or intervention.
4:30.prayer: Father, stretch out Your hand in power and mercy. Work through the name of Your holy Servant Jesus in ways beyond my strength, so that others may see and know Him. Make me prayerful, not merely busy. Amen.

4:31.devotion: God answered the believers' prayer dramatically: the meeting place was shaken, they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and they spoke God's word with boldness. The very grace they asked for was granted, and their fear gave way to Spirit-empowered witness.
4:31.reflection: Where in my life do I need the Holy Spirit to fill me afresh with courage to live and speak for Christ?
4:31.action: Before a task or conversation that intimidates you, pause and ask the Holy Spirit for boldness right then.
4:31.prayer: Lord, fill me with Your Holy Spirit again today. Where I have been silent out of fear, give me boldness; where I have been empty, fill me with Your presence. Let my words and life point to Jesus. Amen.

4:32.devotion: Luke describes the early church's remarkable unity: the believers were of one heart and one soul, and they held their possessions so loosely that they shared freely with one another. Their common life in Christ overflowed into generous, practical community.
4:32.reflection: How loosely do I hold my possessions, and how deeply do I share life with other believers?
4:32.action: Share something concretely today—time, a meal, a skill, or a resource—with a fellow believer in need.
4:32.prayer: Father, make me one in heart and soul with Your people. Deliver me from clinging to what I own, and teach me the joy of generous, open-handed love within Your family. Shape our churches into true community. Amen.

4:33.devotion: With great power the apostles testified to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and great grace rested on them all. The church's witness and the church's grace went together: bold proclamation of Christ's rising was matched by a community marked by God's favor.
4:33.reflection: Is my witness to the resurrection accompanied by a life others can see God's grace upon?
4:33.action: Tell one person today, in a natural way, what the hope of Jesus' resurrection means to you.
4:33.prayer: Risen Lord, give me great grace and great power to bear witness to Your resurrection—not with force, but with love and truth. Let my words and my community together show the world that You are alive. Amen.

4:34.devotion: Because believers sold property and laid the proceeds at the apostles' feet for distribution, there were no needy persons among them. This extraordinary generosity was voluntary, Spirit-driven care within the church, ensuring that no member of the family of God went without.
4:34.reflection: What am I willing to release—financially or otherwise—so that no brother or sister lacks what they need?
4:34.action: Identify one practical need around you this week and give toward it sacrificially, even in a small way.
4:34.prayer: Generous Father, You have given me everything in Christ. Free me from hoarding what You have entrusted to me, and use my resources so that no one in Your family goes without. Make me cheerful and practical in giving. Amen.

4:35.devotion: In the earliest days of the church, believers who owned land or houses sold them and brought the proceeds to the apostles. The money was then shared so that no one in the community went without. This verse captures a church marked by generosity, trust, and practical care for the vulnerable among them.
4:35.reflection: Whose need has God placed near me that I could help meet this week?
4:35.action: Set aside something of value or money today and give it toward meeting a specific, known need in your church or community.
4:35.prayer: Lord, make me generous the way Your early church was generous. Open my eyes to real needs around me, loosen my grip on what I own, and let my giving bring practical help and glory to You. Amen.

4:36.devotion: Luke introduces a man named Joses, whom the apostles nicknamed Barnabas, meaning Son of Encouragement. He was a Levite from Cyprus. His new name reflected his character. In the verses that follow, Barnabas models generous, cheerful giving that strengthened the whole church family.
4:36.reflection: Would the people who know me best call me an encourager?
4:36.action: Contact someone who is discouraged today and speak a specific, sincere word of encouragement to them by text, call, or in person.
4:36.prayer: Father, thank You for encouragers like Barnabas. Shape my character so that my words lift others toward You. Help me notice the weary and hurting today, and use me to strengthen their faith. Amen.

4:37.devotion: Barnabas sold a field he owned and brought the entire sum to the apostles, laying it at their feet. His gift stands as a vivid example of the voluntary generosity described in this passage, and it contrasts with what follows in chapter 5, where giving became a matter of appearance.
4:37.reflection: Is there something I am holding back that God is asking me to release?
4:37.action: Review your finances today and choose one area where you can give freely and privately, without seeking recognition from anyone.
4:37.prayer: Lord, thank You for Barnabas's open-handed example. Teach me to give freely, not for praise but from love. Whatever You have placed in my care, help me hold it loosely and use it for Your purposes. Amen.

5:1.devotion: Chapter 5 opens with a sharp contrast to Barnabas's gift. Ananias and his wife Sapphira sold a possession and presented part of the proceeds as if it were the whole amount. The narrative turn from generous giving to deceptive giving warns readers that God cares about the heart behind our offerings.
5:1.reflection: Am I more concerned with how my giving looks than with whether it is honest?
5:1.action: Examine one area of your life today where image and reality differ, and take one honest step, such as a confession or correction, toward integrity.
5:1.prayer: Search me, O God, and expose any dishonesty in my heart. I do not want to perform generosity for others while hiding the truth from You. Make me truthful in giving, speaking, and living. Amen.

5:2.devotion: Ananias brought only a portion of the money while presenting it as the full price, and Sapphira knew of the deception. The sin was not partial giving, which Peter affirms was permissible, but pretense. They sought the reputation of total generosity without the reality of it.
5:2.reflection: Where am I tempted to appear more devoted or generous than I truly am?
5:2.action: Choose one act of service or giving today and do it quietly, telling no one, letting God alone see and reward it.
5:2.prayer: Father, forgive me for the times I have wanted credit for devotion I do not possess. Free me from the fear of others' opinions, and give me a heart that is content to serve You in secret. Amen.

5:3.devotion: Peter, given discernment in this moment, names the true nature of Ananias's act: lying to the Holy Spirit, influenced by Satan. The offense was not against the apostles but against God Himself. The verse reminds us that the Holy Spirit is divine and that deceit in the church is no small thing.
5:3.reflection: Do I take seriously that my private choices are made before the living God?
5:3.action: Before making any decision today, pause and pray briefly, inviting the Holy Spirit to search your motives and guide your words truthfully.
5:3.prayer: Holy Spirit, thank You for Your presence and holiness. Guard my heart from subtle deception and from the enemy's whispers. Give me discernment to recognize temptation quickly and courage to choose truth, even when it costs me. Amen.

5:4.devotion: Peter makes clear that Ananias was under no obligation. Before the sale the land was his, and after it the money was still under his control. The sin was not keeping money but lying about it. This passage distinguishes voluntary generosity from compulsory giving, exposing hypocrisy rather than requiring believers to surrender all property.
5:4.reflection: Am I honest with God about what I am keeping, rather than pretending I have given it all?
5:4.action: Write down honestly today what you have chosen to keep for yourself, then bring that list to God in prayer without excuses.
5:4.prayer: Lord, You never demanded what was mine to give; You ask for honesty and a willing heart. Forgive my pretenses. Teach me to be truthful before You about my resources, my time, and my motives. Amen.

5:5.devotion: Upon hearing Peter's words, Ananias fell down and died, and great fear came upon all who heard of it. This is a narrative account of divine judgment in a unique founding moment of the church, underscoring God's holiness. It calls readers to reverent awe, not to fear that God strikes down every sinner, for His grace abounds in Christ.
5:5.reflection: Do I approach God with genuine reverence, or have I grown casual about His holiness?
5:5.action: Spend five minutes today in quiet reverence before God, confessing sin specifically and thanking Him for grace offered through Christ.
5:5.prayer: Holy God, this account of judgment awakens my reverence for You. Thank You that through Jesus Your mercy meets Your holiness. Keep me from treating sin lightly, and let awe of You shape how I worship, give, and live. Amen.

5:6.devotion: This verse comes from the sobering account of Ananias and Sapphira, who lied about their giving to appear more generous than they were. After Ananias dies, the young men of the church quietly and respectfully bury him. The narrative reminds us that God takes honesty seriously, and that the early community cared for even the difficult moments with dignity.
5:6.reflection: When have I been tempted to appear more generous or spiritual than I truly am?
5:6.action: Choose one area of your life today where you have been managing an image, and speak or act with simple honesty instead.
5:6.prayer: Lord, You see my heart clearly. Forgive me for the times I have cared more about appearances than truth. Make me honest before You and others, and let my giving and living flow from sincerity. Amen.

5:7.devotion: Three hours after her husband's death, Sapphira arrives unaware of what has happened. Luke's detail slows the story down and shows that she is given her own opportunity to speak truthfully. She is not treated as an afterthought; her own choice and her own answer matter in this account.
5:7.reflection: If someone asked me today to tell the whole truth about a decision I made, what would I say?
5:7.action: Before evening, tell one trusted person the unpolished truth about a struggle or choice you have been softening.
5:7.prayer: Father, thank You that You deal with each of us personally and give us space to be truthful. Help me not to hide behind half-truths, but to walk in Your light with a candid heart. Amen.

5:8.devotion: Peter gives Sapphira a direct, simple question: did you sell the land for this amount? Her answer confirms the agreed-upon lie. The moment shows that deception was a joint choice, and that truth was within her reach. Peter's probing is not entrapment but a clear invitation to honesty that she declines.
5:8.reflection: Am I prepared to answer a straightforward question about my finances or motives without adjusting the truth?
5:8.action: Review one commitment or number you recently reported—money, hours, or effort—and correct it if it was exaggerated.
5:8.prayer: Lord, give me courage for plain answers. When questions come close to my compromises, let me not cling to the lie but confess it. Keep my words and my records truthful before You. Amen.

5:9.devotion: Peter names the heart issue: Sapphira had agreed with her husband to test the Spirit of the Lord. Their sin was not withholding money—giving was voluntary—but lying to God and to the church. This ancient narrative shows how seriously God regards the integrity of His people, not a license to judge others harshly today.
5:9.reflection: Where might I be testing God, assuming He will overlook a compromise I have quietly planned?
5:9.action: Identify one agreement or habit in your closest relationship that dishonors God, and begin renouncing it today.
5:9.prayer: Holy God, forgive me for the compromises I have made with others that grieve Your Spirit. I do not want to test You. Purify my motives and my partnerships so that our shared life honors You alone. Amen.

5:10.devotion: Sapphira also dies, and the young men bury her beside her husband. The severity startles modern readers; it belongs to this unique founding moment of the church, when God guarded its holiness at the outset. The passage calls us to reverence, not fear of arbitrary judgment, and to treat sin with seriousness.
5:10.reflection: Do I treat sin in my life as a small matter, or with the seriousness God gives it?
5:10.action: Spend ten minutes in honest self-examination, confess one specific sin, and take one step of repentance today.
5:10.prayer: Father, this account sobered the early church; let it sober me too. I do not want to treat Your holiness lightly. Search me, expose what needs confessing, and lead me into genuine repentance and peace. Amen.

5:11.devotion: The result of these events was great fear upon the church and all who heard. This is reverent awe, not terror: the believers recognized that God was truly present among them. Healthy reverence guards a community from drifting into casualness about sin and keeps worship grounded in who God is.
5:11.reflection: When did I last feel genuine awe at God's holiness, and what has made my reverence grow dull?
5:11.action: Set aside fifteen minutes today for quiet worship, focusing specifically on God's holiness and your need for His grace.
5:11.prayer: Lord, restore my awe. I confess I can grow casual with You, treating holy things as ordinary. Remind me that You are God and I am not. Let reverence shape my worship and my daily walk. Amen.

5:12.devotion: Alongside the sobering judgment, Luke shows the church's continuing life: many signs and wonders done through the apostles, and believers gathered in unity at Solomon's Porch. The community that learned to fear God also experienced His power and maintained togetherness. Holiness and unity were not opposites but companions.
5:12.reflection: Am I pursuing both reverence and unity, or am I settling for one without the other?
5:12.action: Reach out to a fellow believer today—share a prayer need or pray together—to strengthen unity in your church community.
5:12.prayer: God of power and peace, thank You for the example of a church united in worship and witness. Keep me in harmony with Your people, and use my life, however quietly, to point others to Your work. Amen.

5:13.devotion: Outsiders held back from casually joining the apostles, yet respected them highly. The church's holiness created both a boundary and a reputation. People could not treat this community lightly, but they could not dismiss it either. A church marked by reverent integrity earns a kind of respect that spectacle cannot manufacture.
5:13.reflection: Would outsiders see anything distinctively reverent and trustworthy in the way I live as a Christian?
5:13.action: Perform one unnoticed act of integrity today—at work, home, or online—that reflects Christ even if no one applauds.
5:13.prayer: Father, make my life and my church worthy of respect—not through show, but through integrity, love, and reverence for You. Draw those watching from a distance closer to Christ through what they see in us. Amen.

5:14.devotion: Luke continues his account of the early church in Jerusalem. Even after the sobering story of Ananias and Sapphira, God kept adding believers to the community. The growth is described not simply as joining a group but as being added to the Lord Himself, drawing men and women alike into living relationship with Christ.
5:14.reflection: Am I growing in my sense that belonging to the church means belonging first to the Lord?
5:14.action: Thank God today for one person He has added to your life of faith, and send them a word of encouragement.
5:14.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You that Your church grows by Your grace. Add to Your people daily, and help me welcome every believer, man or woman, as a treasured member of Your body. Keep me rooted in You. Amen.

5:15.devotion: As the apostles' ministry became widely known, people in Jerusalem carried their sick into the streets, hoping even Peter's passing shadow might touch them. Luke records the depth of their longing and hope. Scripture here describes the people's faith and expectation; the healing work itself is attributed to God acting through the apostles.
5:15.reflection: When I or those I love are suffering, do I bring my longing honestly to God rather than hiding it?
5:15.action: Pray today for someone who is ill, asking God for His mercy and comfort in their situation.
5:15.prayer: Father, You see every sick person laid out in hope. I bring You the suffering people I know, asking for Your mercy, healing, and peace according to Your will. Teach me to carry others' burdens faithfully. Amen.

5:16.devotion: Word spread beyond Jerusalem. Crowds came from surrounding towns bringing those who were sick or oppressed by evil spirits, and Luke summarizes that all were healed. This passage describes the extraordinary signs accompanying the apostles' witness in that foundational season of the church, displaying God's compassion and power.
5:16.reflection: Do I believe God still cares deeply about every form of brokenness people carry today?
5:16.action: Ask God to use you this week to show compassion to someone weighed down by suffering or spiritual struggle.
5:16.prayer: Lord, You welcomed the multitudes who came with every kind of affliction. Thank You that You still welcome all who come to You. Make me part of a community where the hurting find compassion, hope, and help. Amen.

5:17.devotion: The church's growth and the apostles' popularity provoked the high priest and the Sadducees, a group that denied resurrection, to jealousy and indignation. The gospel's success threatened their religious authority. This verse shows that faithful witness often stirs opposition, especially from those whose power feels endangered by God's work.
5:17.reflection: When I feel threatened by someone else's success or God's work in their life, how do I respond?
5:17.action: Identify one jealousy you've felt lately, confess it to God, and thank Him for the good thing He gave that person.
5:17.prayer: Father, guard my heart from jealousy when You bless others. Forgive me for the times I have resented Your work instead of rejoicing in it. Give me a humble, glad heart that celebrates Your grace wherever it appears. Amen.

5:18.devotion: In their indignation, the authorities arrested the apostles and imprisoned them in the common jail. This was unjust persecution for preaching the resurrection of Jesus. Luke records this opposition honestly, showing that obedience to Christ can carry real costs, and setting the stage for God's deliverance in the verses that follow.
5:18.reflection: Am I prepared to keep following Jesus even when faithfulness brings misunderstanding or trouble?
5:18.action: Write down one way following Jesus costs you something, and ask God for courage to remain faithful in it.
5:18.prayer: Lord Jesus, You warned that following You could bring opposition. When I face misunderstanding or trouble for my faith, steady my heart. Help me trust that You remain sovereign even behind locked doors, and keep me faithful. Amen.

5:19.devotion: God intervened during the night: an angel of the Lord opened the prison doors and brought the apostles out. This was no escape plan of their own making but divine rescue. Luke shows that the authorities could lock up the messengers, but no prison could restrain the message God had commissioned them to carry.
5:19.reflection: Where in my life do I need to remember that God's purposes are not stopped by human opposition?
5:19.action: Recall one situation that feels like a locked door in your life, and consciously entrust it to God in prayer today.
5:19.prayer: God of deliverance, thank You that no barrier can frustrate Your purposes. When circumstances feel locked against me, remind me that You hold every door. Free me from fear, and send me wherever You want Your word to go. Amen.

5:20.devotion: The angel's command is striking: go back to the temple, the very place of danger, and speak to the people all the words of this life. Deliverance came with a mission. The apostles were freed not for safety but for proclamation. The gospel is literally called a message of life, good news centered on the risen Christ.
5:20.reflection: Has God given me words of life that I have been keeping to myself out of fear?
5:20.action: Share one sentence of gospel hope with someone today, whether in person, by text, or in a note.
5:20.prayer: Lord, You rescued Your servants and sent them straight back to speak the words of this life. Give me that same courage and clarity. Use my ordinary words today to point someone toward the life found in You. Amen.

5:21.devotion: The apostles obeyed immediately, entering the temple at dawn to teach, while the council assembled and sent officers to fetch prisoners who were no longer there. The contrast is vivid: bold early-morning obedience on one side, bewildered official power on the other. God's word moved forward while human opposition scrambled to catch up.
5:21.reflection: When God gives me a clear instruction, do I respond promptly or wait for circumstances to feel safer?
5:21.action: Complete today one act of obedience you have been postponing, however small, and do it early in your day.
5:21.prayer: Father, Your servants rose at dawn to do what You said. Make me quick to obey, not cautious, delayed, or afraid. Let my mornings begin with You, and let my obedience outpace every obstacle that stands in the way. Amen.

5:22.devotion: After the apostles were freed from prison by an angel, the officers arrived to fetch them for the council—only to find the cell empty. This passage describes a moment of confusion for the authorities, while readers of Acts know God had opened the doors. What looked impossible to the guards was already accomplished by God.
5:22.reflection: Where might God already be working in a situation I have written off as closed or hopeless?
5:22.action: Identify one situation today you consider locked shut, and pray specifically about it, asking God to work in His way and timing.
5:22.prayer: Lord, You are not limited by locked doors or human barriers. Where I see only dead ends, help me trust that You are actively working. Open my eyes to Your power and keep my heart hopeful in You. Amen.

5:23.devotion: The officers gave a careful report: everything appeared in order—doors locked, guards at their posts—yet the prisoners were gone. Their account highlights the thoroughness of the security and, by contrast, the completeness of God's deliverance. Sometimes faithful obedience is verified by what others cannot explain.
5:23.reflection: When God's work in my life defies explanation, do I give Him credit or search for a natural explanation first?
5:23.action: Recall one unexplained provision or protection in your life, and thank God for it aloud or in your journal today.
5:23.prayer: Father, thank You that Your deliverance is complete and Your care is real, even when I cannot explain it. Teach me to recognize Your hand and give You glory for the good things only You could do. Amen.

5:24.devotion: The high priest, temple captain, and chief priests were bewildered by the report and uncertain where events would lead. Luke shows the religious leaders struggling to control a movement they could not understand or stop. Their confusion contrasts with the apostles' settled confidence in God's mission.
5:24.reflection: When circumstances confuse me, am I seeking human control, or resting in God's larger purposes?
5:24.action: Name one current situation that puzzles or unsettles you, and consciously release the outcome to God in a short written prayer.
5:24.prayer: Gracious God, You hold outcomes that puzzle and unsettle me. When I cannot see what will happen next, anchor my heart in Your wisdom and goodness. Help me rest in Your purposes rather than grasping for control. Amen.

5:25.devotion: While the leaders puzzled over the empty cell, news arrived that the apostles were publicly teaching in the temple—the very activity they had been arrested for. God's deliverance was not merely an escape; it restored the apostles to their mission. Freedom in Scripture often serves witness, not comfort alone.
5:25.reflection: Has God's rescue or blessing in my life led me back to His purposes, or only to my own comfort?
5:25.action: Consider one way God has freed or blessed you, and use part of today to serve or encourage someone else with it.
5:25.prayer: Lord, thank You that Your gifts and rescues in my life are meant to bear fruit, not just bring me ease. Redirect my gratitude into service. Show me today whom I can encourage or help in Your name. Amen.

5:26.devotion: The captain and officers retrieved the apostles carefully, avoiding force because they feared the crowd might stone them. This detail shows the leaders' weakened position: the people highly respected the apostles. God's favor on His servants was evident even to those opposing them.
5:26.reflection: Is my conduct among others so gracious that even those who disagree with me treat me with respect?
5:26.action: Interact today with one person who differs from you—speak with kindness and patience rather than defensiveness or argument.
5:26.prayer: Father, make my life honorable so that even critics see Your grace in me. Guard me from harshness and help me win people with patience and love, as Your servants did. May my conduct point others to You. Amen.

5:27.devotion: The apostles were brought before the Sanhedrin, the same council that had condemned Jesus, and the high priest began his questioning. This was an intimidating setting: the highest religious authority confronting ordinary men. Luke prepares us for the apostles' bold answer by showing the weight of the opposition they faced.
5:27.reflection: When I face intimidating authority or pressure, does fear silence me, or does faith steady my voice?
5:27.action: Identify one truth you have been hesitant to voice because of pressure, and share it graciously with someone today.
5:27.prayer: Lord Jesus, You faced hostile councils with courage, and You stand with Your people in intimidating moments. When pressure mounts, steady my heart and my words. Give me humility to speak Your truth with grace and without fear. Amen.

5:28.devotion: The high priest accused the apostles of defying the ban on teaching in Jesus' name and of spreading their message throughout Jerusalem. He framed the gospel as an attempt to blame the leaders for Jesus' death. The accusation itself testifies to how rapidly and widely the apostles' witness had spread.
5:28.reflection: If someone summarized the influence of my life, would they say I have filled my circle with the message of Christ?
5:28.action: Choose one simple, natural way today to share your faith with someone—a testimony, an invitation, or a spiritual conversation.
5:28.prayer: Father, the apostles' witness filled Jerusalem; let my witness fill my home, workplace, and neighborhood. Give me courage to speak of Jesus naturally and faithfully, and use my small efforts for Your great purposes. Amen.

5:29.devotion: Peter answered the council with a principle that has guided believers ever since: when human authority commands what God forbids, or forbids what God commands, allegiance to God comes first. This was not disrespect for all authority, but faithfulness when the two loyalties collided. The apostles spoke respectfully yet stood firm.
5:29.reflection: Is there an area where pressure from people is tempting me to compromise what God has clearly asked of me?
5:29.action: Write down one area of potential compromise you face, and decide today, in prayer, to follow God's way regardless of cost.
5:29.prayer: Father, give me the apostles' courage to honor You above every human pressure. Keep me respectful toward authority, yet unwavering in obedience to You. Strengthen me to stand faithfully, trusting You with whatever consequences follow. Amen.

5:30.devotion: Standing before the Sanhedrin, Peter does not soften the truth. He declares that the God of Israel raised Jesus from the dead, even though the council's leaders had handed Him over to die on a cross. The resurrection confronts human rejection with God's vindication.
5:30.reflection: How do I respond when the truth about Jesus challenges my comfort or reputation?
5:30.action: Speak a simple, honest word about Jesus to someone today, even if it feels awkward.
5:30.prayer: Lord, You raised Jesus although people rejected Him. Give me courage to acknowledge Him plainly, trusting that Your truth stands stronger than my fear or anyone's disapproval.

5:31.devotion: Peter proclaims that the crucified Jesus is now exalted at God's right hand as Prince and Savior. His exaltation is not merely for honor but for giving: repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins. The Risen Lord actively offers grace.
5:31.reflection: Have I brought my need for repentance and forgiveness to the exalted Savior Himself?
5:31.action: Name one sin honestly before God today and receive His forgiveness with thanksgiving rather than lingering in shame.
5:31.prayer: Prince and Savior, thank You that Your throne is a fountain of mercy. Lead me to genuine repentance, and help me live today in the freedom of Your forgiveness.

5:32.devotion: Peter says the apostles are witnesses to the risen, exalted Christ, and the Holy Spirit is a witness too, given by God to those who obey Him. Testimony and the Spirit's inner confirmation go together in proclaiming the gospel.
5:32.reflection: In what area of my life is the Spirit prompting me toward obedience right now?
5:32.action: Choose one act of obedience you have been delaying, and do it today as an act of faith.
5:32.prayer: Holy Spirit, thank You for bearing witness to Jesus in my heart. Help me obey You promptly, so my life and words both point others to the risen Lord.

5:33.devotion: When the council heard Peter's words, they were cut to the heart—but instead of repenting, they burned with fury and plotted to kill the apostles. This verse honestly shows that truth can harden hearts when pride resists conviction.
5:33.reflection: When God's truth convicts me, do I respond with humility or with defensiveness and anger?
5:33.action: Notice today when someone's words sting you, and pause to ask God whether He is correcting you before reacting.
5:33.prayer: Father, soften my heart when conviction comes. Guard me from the fury that resists truth, and give me the humility to receive Your correction with a repentant, teachable spirit.

5:34.devotion: Amid the council's rage, Gamaliel, a respected Pharisaic teacher of the law, rises with a cooler head. He orders the apostles removed from the room so the council can deliberate. God can use even a cautious voice to restrain violence against His servants.
5:34.reflection: When tensions rise around me, am I willing to be a calm voice that slows things down?
5:34.action: If a heated conversation arises today, step back and help everyone pause before speaking or deciding in anger.
5:34.prayer: Lord, thank You for raising up calm voices in moments of fury. Make me steady under pressure, willing to pause, listen, and protect others from harm caused by hasty anger.

5:35.devotion: Gamaliel urges his colleagues to careful self-examination: take heed to yourselves what you intend to do regarding these men. Before acting against the apostles, he calls the council to weigh their motives and their actions soberly.
5:35.reflection: Do I examine my own intentions before acting against someone, or do I rush to judgment?
5:35.action: Before making a hard decision about a person today, write down your real motives and pray over them first.
5:35.prayer: Father, teach me to take heed to myself before judging others. Search my intentions, slow my judgments, and let my decisions reflect wisdom and fairness rather than impulse.

5:36.devotion: Gamaliel recalls Theudas, who claimed to be somebody and gathered about four hundred followers, but was slain and his movement scattered and brought to nothing. His point: movements founded on human claims often collapse when the leader falls.
5:36.reflection: Am I building my life on a person or cause that will fade, or on Christ who endures?
5:36.action: Identify one place you are seeking significance outside of Christ, and consciously surrender that to God today.
5:36.prayer: Lord, keep me from chasing the passing causes and hollow promises of this world. Anchor my hope in Your kingdom alone, which lasts when everything else comes to nothing.

5:37.devotion: Gamaliel gives a second example: Judas of Galilee, who rose during the days of the census and drew away many followers, yet perished, and his followers were dispersed. Human uprisings, however impressive, scatter when their leaders die—unlike the movement of the risen Christ.
5:37.reflection: Where do I place my confidence— in human strength and numbers, or in the living Lord?
5:37.action: Thank God in writing today for one way His kingdom has endured in your life beyond circumstances or people.
5:37.prayer: Father, human movements rise and scatter, but Your church stands because Jesus lives. Keep my faith fixed on Him, not on charisma, numbers, or the strength of any leader.

5:38.devotion: Gamaliel, a respected teacher, counsels the Sanhedrin to release the apostles rather than punish them. His argument: human movements fizzle out on their own. Though he speaks as a cautious Pharisee, his words remind us that God's purposes do not depend on human defense or approval to endure.
5:38.reflection: Am I trying to secure God's work by my own strength instead of trusting Him with it?
5:38.action: Release one worry about a ministry or witness situation today, praying instead of striving to control the outcome.
5:38.prayer: Father, thank You that Your work does not rest on my shoulders. Free me from anxiety about outcomes, and teach me to trust that Your purposes stand firm. Help me serve faithfully and leave the results to You. Amen.

5:39.devotion: Gamaliel completes his counsel with a sober warning: if the apostles' movement is from God, the council cannot overturn it, and opposing it would mean fighting against God. Even an unbelieving voice in Scripture points to a lasting truth—nothing and no one can thwart what God has purposed to do.
5:39.reflection: Where might my resistance to something be resistance to God Himself?
5:39.action: Examine one area where you have resisted God's direction, and write a one-line prayer surrendering it to Him today.
5:39.prayer: Lord, keep my heart soft and humble. If I am resisting Your will anywhere, reveal it gently and give me courage to yield. I do not want to fight against You; I want to walk with You. Amen.

5:40.devotion: The council takes Gamaliel's advice in part: they release the apostles, but not before beating them and forbidding them to speak in Jesus' name. It is a compromise—mercy mixed with hostility. The apostles walk away marked by wounds, yet the gospel continues, for threats cannot silence what grace has commissioned.
5:40.reflection: How do I respond when obedience to Christ costs me something real?
5:40.action: Identify one place where you have stayed quiet about your faith out of fear, and share a simple word of testimony there this week.
5:40.prayer: Lord Jesus, You never promised that following You would be painless. Strengthen me when I face criticism or loss for Your name, and keep my voice faithful. Help me honor You even when it is costly. Amen.

5:41.devotion: Strangely, the apostles leave the council rejoicing. They are not glad that pain exists, but that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for Jesus' name. Their joy flows from identification with Him. What the council intended as humiliation, they received as an honor—a badge of belonging to Christ.
5:41.reflection: Do I see identification with Jesus as an honor, even when it brings embarrassment or loss?
5:41.action: Thank God today, in writing or aloud, for one specific way you have been identified with Christ, even if it felt costly.
5:41.prayer: Jesus, reshape how I see hardship for Your sake. Turn my instinct to avoid embarrassment into gratitude for belonging to You. Give me joy that does not depend on comfort, but on being Yours. Amen.

5:42.devotion: Undeterred, the apostles resume their rhythm of ministry—daily in the temple courts and from house to house, teaching and preaching Jesus as the Christ. Persecution interrupted neither their message nor their consistency. The gospel advanced not through one dramatic moment, but through steady, everyday faithfulness.
5:42.reflection: Is my witness a one-time event or a daily rhythm?
5:42.action: Choose one recurring daily moment—morning coffee, a commute, a meal—and use it this week for prayer or a word about Jesus.
5:42.prayer: Father, make me faithful in the ordinary. Let me not wait for big occasions to speak of Jesus, but weave witness into my daily life. Give me persistence that hardship cannot interrupt. Amen.

6:1.devotion: As the church grows, a real problem surfaces: Greek-speaking widows are being overlooked in the daily food distribution while Hebrew widows are served. Growth exposes gaps. Scripture records this honestly—the early church was not flawless, and faithful care for the vulnerable, especially widows, was essential to its witness.
6:1.reflection: Who in my community might be quietly overlooked or underserved?
6:1.action: Notice one person who is easily overlooked in your church or neighborhood, and take a practical step to include or help them today.
6:1.prayer: Lord, open my eyes to those I have overlooked. Forgive me where I have shown favoritism or inattention. Give Your church generous, impartial care for the vulnerable, and make me part of that care. Amen.

6:2.devotion: The twelve gather the whole community rather than fixing the issue quietly. They acknowledge that abandoning prayer and the ministry of the word to manage distributions would not be right. Their answer is not that serving tables is beneath anyone, but that the church needs both proclamation and practical care, each done faithfully.
6:2.reflection: Am I trying to carry responsibilities God has assigned to others in the body of Christ?
6:2.action: Name your primary calling or gifting, and say no to one task today that distracts from it, entrusting it to someone else.
6:2.prayer: Father, thank You for giving every member of Your church a role. Help me honor others' callings while being faithful to my own. Guard me from busyness that crowds out prayer and Your word. Amen.

6:3.devotion: The apostles ask the congregation to select seven men of good reputation, full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom, to oversee the daily distribution. Spiritual maturity, not mere availability, qualifies people for service—even in practical matters. The church involves the whole community in choosing leaders, and character stands at the center.
6:3.reflection: Would others describe me as Spirit-filled and wise in the practical service I give?
6:3.action: Ask a trusted friend today which quality—reputation, Spirit-ledness, or wisdom—you should grow in most, and thank them for their honesty.
6:3.prayer: Holy Spirit, fill me afresh. Grow in me the character that serves well—honesty, wisdom, and love. Use me in practical tasks as truly as in spiritual ones, and let my service reflect Christ. Amen.

6:4.devotion: When a practical need in the early church threatened to distract the apostles, they proposed a solution that would free them for two priorities: prayer and teaching God's word. Their commitment reminds us that serving others well includes guarding time for communion with God and the ministry of Scripture.
6:4.reflection: Is there something filling my schedule that is quietly crowding out prayer and time in God's word?
6:4.action: Set aside fifteen minutes today specifically for prayer and reading Scripture, and protect that time as an appointment you cannot cancel.
6:4.prayer: Lord, help me honor You as the apostles did, giving myself continually to prayer and to Your word. Guard my priorities, and let communion with You shape everything I do today. In Jesus' name, amen.

6:5.devotion: The whole congregation agreed with the apostles' proposal and chose seven men to serve. Stephen stands out as a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit, showing that practical service in the church is spiritual work carried out by spiritually rich people.
6:5.reflection: Do I ask God to fill me with faith and the Spirit for the ordinary tasks He gives me, not just the visible ones?
6:5.action: Do one humble service task today, such as helping a neighbor or church worker, and pray beforehand for the Spirit's presence in it.
6:5.prayer: Father, make me like Stephen, full of faith and Your Holy Spirit. Prepare me for every task You place before me, whether seen or unseen, and let my service flow from a heart devoted to You. Amen.

6:6.devotion: The chosen servants were brought before the apostles, who prayed and laid hands on them. This act publicly set them apart for their ministry, showing that the church entrusted important work to God's blessing and recognized those who would serve with dignity.
6:6.reflection: When I begin a new responsibility, do I pause to pray over it, or do I simply rush into the work?
6:6.action: Before starting your work or tasks today, briefly pray, asking God to bless and guide your service throughout the day.
6:6.prayer: Lord, thank You for the example of a church that prayed before appointing servants. Teach me to seek Your blessing over my work and responsibilities, dedicating each one to You before I begin. In Jesus' name, amen.

6:7.devotion: As the church worked together in prayer, the word, and practical service, the gospel spread rapidly and many disciples were added in Jerusalem, including many priests who came to obedient faith. Healthy, united ministry bore remarkable fruit for God's kingdom.
6:7.reflection: Am I contributing to the unity and health of my church community, or am I holding back from playing my part?
6:7.action: Find one way to support your church's ministry this week, such as volunteering, encouraging a leader, or inviting someone to a service.
6:7.prayer: Father, bless Your church so that Your word spreads widely and many come to obedient faith in Jesus. Use my small part in the body for Your larger purposes, and keep us united in serving You. Amen.

6:8.devotion: Stephen had been chosen for a serving role, yet God equipped him for far more. Scripture points to two qualities that marked him: faith and power. His trust in God, strengthened by the Spirit, was not private comfort only—it overflowed publicly as wonders and signs that drew people's attention to God. Spiritual fullness, not title or position, qualified him for this work.
6:8.reflection: Would people around me recognize faith and God's power at work in my everyday responsibilities?
6:8.action: Pick one ordinary task today and do it while asking God to work through it with faith and visible power.
6:8.prayer: Lord, fill me with the same faith and power that marked Stephen. Work through my serving, my words, and my daily life so others see Your wonders and turn their hearts toward You. Amen.

6:9.devotion: Stephen's Spirit-filled ministry drew opposition. Members of a synagogue of Freedmen from several regions disputed with him. This verse honestly shows that faithful witness can provoke disagreement, as the gospel challenged long-held assumptions and traditions.
6:9.reflection: When my faith meets disagreement or pushback, do I respond with grace and courage, or do I shrink back?
6:9.action: Write down one belief you hold that others sometimes challenge, and prepare a kind, respectful way to explain it if asked.
6:9.prayer: Lord Jesus, You promised that following You would bring some opposition. Give me courage to stand for truth and grace to speak gently when my faith is disputed. Keep me faithful under pressure. Amen.

6:10.devotion: Stephen's opponents could not withstand the wisdom and the Spirit by which he spoke. His effectiveness came not from clever argument alone but from God's Spirit working through a man full of faith, an encouragement for anyone called to testify about Christ.
6:10.reflection: Do I rely on my own abilities when sharing my faith, or do I ask the Spirit for wisdom?
6:10.action: Before any conversation today where you might discuss faith, silently ask the Holy Spirit to give you wisdom and gentle words.
6:10.prayer: Holy Spirit, fill me with the wisdom that comes from You. When I speak about Jesus, let my words carry Your truth and gentleness, and remind me that my strength is in You, not myself. Amen.

6:11.devotion: Unable to answer Stephen openly, his opponents secretly recruited men to make false accusations of blasphemy against him. This verse exposes how opposition to the truth can turn to dishonesty, and it reminds believers that God's word judges deceit even when it targets the innocent.
6:11.reflection: Have I ever been tempted to twist the truth or pass along a rumor about someone I disagree with?
6:11.action: Refuse to repeat any unverified story about a person today, and if you hear one, gently ask whether it is actually true.
6:11.prayer: Father, guard my tongue from falsehood and my heart from deceit. When others misrepresent me or Your truth, help me trust You with the outcome and continue speaking honestly in Your sight. In Jesus' name, amen.

6:12.devotion: Fueled by false accusations, the opponents stirred up the people, elders, and scribes, who seized Stephen and brought him before the council. This ancient account shows how quickly misinformation can escalate, yet Stephen faced it with the faith and Spirit described earlier in the chapter.
6:12.reflection: If I faced unfair treatment for my faith, would I remember that God remains with me in the trial?
6:12.action: Pray today for Christians who face false accusations or hostility for their faith, asking God to give them courage and peace.
6:12.prayer: Lord, You see when Your people are treated unfairly. Stand close to those who suffer for their faith, giving them courage and peace, and keep me steadfast if I ever face opposition for following You. Amen.

6:13.devotion: Stephen, a Spirit-filled servant accused of wrongdoing, now faces hostile testimony. His opponents produce false witnesses, echoing the treatment Jesus himself received. This verse reminds us that faithfulness to God can attract distortion and lies, yet God sees the truth even when human courts do not.
6:13.reflection: When my reputation is misjudged, do I trust God to defend me rather than lash out?
6:13.action: If someone misrepresents you today, pause before responding; answer calmly or choose silence, committing the situation to God in a short prayer.
6:13.prayer: Lord, when I am misunderstood or falsely accused, guard my tongue and my heart. Remind me that You see the truth, and help me respond with the gentleness of Your Spirit. Amen.

6:14.devotion: The accusation twists Stephen's message about Jesus. Like his Lord, Stephen is charged with threatening the temple and the law of Moses. The gospel did indeed point to fulfillment beyond old forms, but the witnesses distort this into destruction. Truth often suffers when people feel their traditions threatened.
6:14.reflection: Am I quick to assume the worst about those whose message challenges my familiar ways?
6:14.action: Identify one person or group whose views unsettle you, and pray for understanding rather than judgment before speaking about them today.
6:14.prayer: Father, forgive me for the times I have misrepresented others or feared change more than I trusted You. Give me discernment to hear truth clearly and grace to receive it. Amen.

6:15.devotion: Facing the council, Stephen's face shines like an angel's, recalling Moses' radiant face. God visibly honors His servant in the moment of accusation. The scene contrasts human hostility with divine peace: the accused one reflects heaven's light while his accusers scheme in darkness.
6:15.reflection: Does my countenance under pressure reflect trust in God, or only my anxiety?
6:15.action: Before a stressful conversation today, take three slow breaths and ask God to let His peace show in your face and words.
6:15.prayer: God of glory, I cannot manufacture peace on my own. Fill me with Your presence so that even in conflict, others may glimpse something of Your calm and light through me. Amen.

7:1.devotion: The high priest's question, "Are these things so?", opens Stephen's defense. Instead of a legal rebuttal, Stephen will answer with the whole story of God's dealings with Israel. Scripture becomes his testimony, showing that his faithfulness to Jesus flows from faithfulness to God's unfolding plan.
7:1.reflection: When asked about my faith, can I tell the story of God's work, or only offer fragments?
7:1.action: Spend ten minutes today reading a portion of Scripture, and write one sentence about how it connects to your own walk with God.
7:1.prayer: Lord, root me so deeply in Your story that Your Word comes naturally to my lips. Help me answer questions about my hope with clarity, humility, and love. Amen.

7:2.devotion: Stephen begins with Abraham, emphasizing that the God of glory appeared in Mesopotamia, before the temple, the land, or the law existed. God's initiative came first. Stephen quietly frames his defense around a God who is not confined to any holy building or place.
7:2.reflection: Do I picture God as bigger than the places and routines where I usually meet Him?
7:2.action: Step outside today, even briefly, and consciously acknowledge God's glory in the open sky or ordinary street around you.
7:2.prayer: God of glory, You met Abraham in a foreign land and You meet me in ordinary places. Widen my vision so I never confine You to buildings or habits. Amen.

7:3.devotion: God called Abraham to leave country, relatives, and comfort, promising to lead him to a land yet to be shown. Faith here means obeying before seeing. Stephen's audience is being invited to recognize that God's people have always been pilgrims, led forward by promise rather than certainty.
7:3.reflection: What might God be asking me to leave behind before He shows me what comes next?
7:3.action: Name one comfort, habit, or possession that competes with your trust in God, and take one small practical step toward loosening your grip on it.
7:3.prayer: Lord, Abraham went out not knowing where he was going, and You guided him. Give me courage to obey Your call step by step, trusting You for the destination. Amen.

7:4.devotion: Abraham's journey unfolded gradually: first to Haran, and only after his father's death into the promised land. God's leading honors His timing. Stephen notes that Abraham did arrive in the very land Stephen's hearers now occupy, grounding his defense in a shared heritage they all claim.
7:4.reflection: Am I willing to let God's timing shape my journey, even when progress seems delayed?
7:4.action: Review one goal you have been impatient about, and write a prayer of trust regarding God's timing for it today.
7:4.prayer: Patient God, You led Abraham by stages, not all at once. Teach me to accept the pauses in my life as part of Your guidance, and to keep walking. Amen.

7:5.devotion: Abraham received no inheritance in the promised land, not even a foot of ground, though God promised it to his descendants. Stephen highlights a life of promise fulfilled beyond sight. God's people are called to trust His word even when fulfillment lies far beyond their own lifetime.
7:5.reflection: Can I trust God's promises even if I never see their completion in my lifetime?
7:5.action: Choose one biblical promise today and write it where you will see it, praying over it once in the morning and once in the evening.
7:5.prayer: Faithful God, Abraham died having seen only beginnings of Your promise, yet he trusted You completely. Strengthen my faith to hold Your word firmly when I cannot yet see its fulfillment. Amen.

7:6.devotion: Stephen, defending his faith before the council, retells God's promise to Abraham. God foretold that Abraham's descendants would live as foreigners and suffer bondage and oppression for four hundred years. Even before Israel existed as a nation, God saw their suffering and woven it into His larger plan of redemption.
7:6.reflection: Where do I struggle to trust that God sees my long, difficult seasons?
7:6.action: Name one hardship that has lasted a long time, and write a note asking God to help you trust Him within it today.
7:6.prayer: Faithful God, You know the length of every trial before it begins. Help me trust Your timing when suffering stretches on, and remind me that You see me and are working purposes I cannot yet understand. Amen.

7:7.devotion: Stephen continues the story: God promised to judge the nation that enslaved His people and to bring them out to worship Him in that very place. Bondage would not be the ending. God's judgment on oppression and His promise of deliverance and worship are woven together in His faithfulness.
7:7.reflection: Do I believe God will act against injustice and bring His people out to worship Him?
7:7.action: Pray today for one group of people facing oppression, asking God for deliverance, and thank Him for one way He has already freed you.
7:7.prayer: Righteous God, You judge oppression and You rescue the bound. We ask You to act for those in bondage today, and teach us to worship You as the God who delivers. Keep our hope anchored in Your promises. Amen.

7:8.devotion: Stephen recalls the covenant of circumcision, the sign God gave Abraham marking His chosen family. The covenant carried through generations: Abraham circumcised Isaac, and the line continued through Jacob to the twelve patriarchs. God's promises were not momentary; they were passed down and preserved through ordinary family generations.
7:8.reflection: How am I helping the faith I hold become a living inheritance for those who come after me?
7:8.action: Share one story of God's faithfulness with a family member or friend today, passing it on in simple conversation.
7:8.prayer: Covenant-keeping God, thank You that Your promises span generations. Help me treasure what You have done and pass it on faithfully, so those who come after me will know You and trust Your word. Amen.

7:9.devotion: Stephen names the hard truth: the patriarchs, out of envy, sold their own brother Joseph into Egypt. Yet human betrayal did not cancel God's presence. The simple, powerful summary stands at the end of the verse—'But God was with him.' Envy harmed Joseph, but it never separated him from God.
7:9.reflection: When envy or resentment has wounded me or come from me, can I still believe God remains present?
7:9.action: Ask God to reveal any envy in your heart today, and take one step toward reconciling with someone you have resented or who has hurt you.
7:9.prayer: Gracious God, envy and betrayal cause real pain, but You remain with the wounded. Search my heart, uproot jealousy, and help me trust that Your presence follows me even through what others mean for harm. Amen.

7:10.devotion: God did not abandon Joseph in his troubles. Stephen tells how God delivered him, granted him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh, and elevated him to governor over Egypt and Pharaoh's household. Joseph's suffering was long, but God's presence led ultimately to rescue, honor, and a role in preserving many lives.
7:10.reflection: Am I asking God for wisdom in my present circumstances, not only rescue from them?
7:10.action: Before one decision today, pause and pray for wisdom, then choose carefully and honestly, trusting God with the outcome.
7:10.prayer: God of deliverance, thank You for staying with Joseph through every trouble and lifting him in Your time. Grant me wisdom for today's decisions, favor where You will, and patience to trust Your rescue. Amen.

7:11.devotion: Stephen moves the story forward: famine and great trouble struck Egypt and Canaan together, and the fathers of Israel found no food. This crisis, severe and widespread, became the very circumstance God used to reunite Joseph with his family and preserve Jacob's line. Need drove God's people toward His provision.
7:11.reflection: When I face seasons of real lack, do I look for where God might be providing?
7:11.action: Identify one practical need in your household or community, and take one honest step toward meeting it, whether by asking for help or offering it.
7:11.prayer: Providing God, famine came, and Your people found no food—yet You had already prepared grain in Egypt. Open my eyes to the provision You have placed around me, and make me willing both to receive and to share. Amen.

7:12.devotion: When Jacob heard there was grain in Egypt, he acted. He sent his sons to seek sustenance for the starving household. Stephen shows the patriarchs as hungry men dependent on help from the very place where their rejected brother held power. Faith did not mean passivity; Jacob heard, believed, and sent.
7:12.reflection: When God makes provision known, am I willing to take the humble step of going to receive it?
7:12.action: Respond today to one opportunity God has already placed before you—a need you have heard of—by taking a first concrete step instead of waiting.
7:12.prayer: Father, Jacob heard of grain and sent his sons. Give me ears to hear where You are providing and the humility to act on what I hear. Teach me to trust You with my family's needs. Amen.

7:13.devotion: On the second visit, Joseph made himself known to his brothers—the moment of revelation after years of concealment—and Joseph's family became known to Pharaoh. What began with betrayal ended with recognition, family restored, and a foreign king hearing of this people. God's hidden work stepped openly into the light.
7:13.reflection: Is there a broken relationship where God may be preparing a moment of honest recognition and restoration?
7:13.action: Take one step toward honesty in a strained relationship today—speak the truth in kindness, or make the first phone call or message.
7:13.prayer: God of restoration, You brought Joseph's hidden identity into the open and his family into Pharaoh's hearing. Bring truth to light in my relationships, heal what betrayal has broken, and let Your quiet work be seen. Amen.

7:14.devotion: In his defense before the Sanhedrin, Stephen recounts how Joseph, exalted in Egypt, summoned his father Jacob and all the family—seventy-five people—to escape famine. What God preserved through Joseph's suffering became the beginning of a nation. Stephen shows that God's saving work often begins small and through unlikely means.
7:14.reflection: Where might God be working preservation and provision in your life right now through circumstances you did not choose?
7:14.action: Reach out to a family member or friend today with a word of gratitude for how God has carried your family through a hard season.
7:14.prayer: Faithful God, thank You for preserving Your people through Joseph's story. Help me trust that You are working even in small beginnings and painful seasons, and keep my heart open to Your quiet provision each day. Amen.

7:15.devotion: Stephen continues Israel's story: Jacob went down to Egypt with his sons, and there the patriarchs died. Even the fathers of the faith died in a land not their own, still awaiting God's promise. Stephen reminds his listeners that the promised inheritance was not yet reality—faith meant trusting God beyond one's own lifetime.
7:15.reflection: Can you hold God's promises with patience, even if you never see their full fulfillment in your own lifetime?
7:15.action: Write down one promise from Scripture you are still waiting on God to fulfill, and commit to praying about it weekly.
7:15.prayer: Lord, Jacob died trusting promises he did not yet see. Teach me that kind of patient faith. When fulfillment seems far away, anchor my hope in Your faithfulness across generations. Amen.

7:16.devotion: Stephen notes that the patriarchs' remains were carried back to Shechem and laid in a tomb Abraham had purchased. Though they died in Egypt, their burial in the promised land testified to hope in God's covenant. Stephen weaves the details of Israel's history to show God's promise advancing step by step.
7:16.reflection: What practices in your life visibly testify that you believe God's promises are real and certain?
7:16.action: Choose one visible act of hope today—such as journaling a prayer, planting something, or writing a note of encouragement—that expresses trust in God's future.
7:16.prayer: God of Abraham, You kept Your people's hope alive even in their deaths. May my ordinary choices reflect that I trust Your promises. Keep my eyes fixed on Your faithful plan. Amen.

7:17.devotion: Stephen explains that as the time of God's sworn promise to Abraham drew near, His people grew and multiplied in Egypt. God's timing and the people's flourishing moved together. Hard years in a foreign land became the setting for remarkable growth, according to God's covenant word rather than human comfort.
7:17.reflection: Do you believe God can be growing you most during seasons that feel like waiting in a strange land?
7:17.action: Identify one difficult season in your past and write down at least one way God grew or provided for you during it.
7:17.prayer: Covenant-keeping God, thank You that Your promises arrive at exactly the right time. When my circumstances feel barren, remind me that You are still at work, growing Your purposes in ways I cannot see. Amen.

7:18.devotion: Stephen recalls that a new king arose in Egypt who did not know Joseph. Memory faded, and with it, favor. The people who had been welcomed became vulnerable when leadership changed.
