This verse reminds us that God sometimes alerts His servants to danger, and that wisdom and vigilance are not signs of weak faith but part of faithful living under pressure.
9:24.reflection: When I face pressure or hostility for my faith, do I respond with prayerful wisdom as well as courage?
9:24.action: Consider one difficult situation you face, and take one prudent, practical step today while praying for God's guidance in it.
9:24.prayer: Lord, You know the pressures I face, seen and unseen. Give me both courage and wisdom, the faith to trust You and the sense to act carefully. Protect Your people, and keep me alert and prayerful. Amen.

9:25.devotion: In a vivid nighttime escape, the disciples lower Saul through the wall in a large basket. The great apostle is saved by ordinary believers working together in the dark. This humble episode shows the body of Christ at its best: believers risking and serving so that God's servant can continue the ministry God gave him.
9:25.reflection: Am I willing to serve in small, unglamorous ways so that others can carry out God's work?
9:25.action: Offer practical help today to someone serving in ministry or facing difficulty, without expecting recognition or thanks.
9:25.prayer: Father, thank You for the quiet servants who hold the ropes, open the doors, and carry the burdens behind the scenes. Make me faithful in small tasks, and help me value every member of Your body. Amen.

9:26.devotion: When Saul arrives in Jerusalem, the disciples are afraid and refuse to believe he is truly a follower of Jesus. Their fear is understandable given his history of persecution. This verse honestly portrays how hard it can be to trust that someone has genuinely changed, even when God has done a deep work in their life.
9:26.reflection: Is there someone I have been unwilling to forgive or trust, even though God may be changing them?
9:26.action: Take one step toward someone you have kept at a distance, perhaps a kind message or conversation, asking God to guide your words.
9:26.prayer: Lord, You change people in ways we struggle to believe. Soften my heart toward those whose past makes me cautious. Give me discernment wrapped in grace, and help me welcome those You have redeemed. Amen.

9:27.devotion: Saul, the former persecutor, had become a believer, but the Jerusalem believers feared him. Barnabas, whose name means son of encouragement, took a risk. He personally brought Saul to the apostles and vouched for his testimony of meeting the risen Lord and preaching boldly in Damascus.
9:27.reflection: Who around you needs someone to stand beside them and vouch for their changed life?
9:27.action: Reach out today to someone who seems isolated or misunderstood, and publicly speak a word of affirmation on their behalf.
9:27.prayer: Lord, make me a Barnabas. Give me courage to welcome those others avoid and to advocate for people trying to follow You after difficult pasts. Let my encouragement build bridges in Your church. Amen.

9:28.devotion: Because Barnabas intervened, Saul was welcomed into the fellowship of the Jerusalem church. He stayed with the believers, sharing ordinary life with them. Acceptance preceded his ministry there; Saul came in and went out among them as one of their own.
9:28.reflection: Do you let new believers into the everyday rhythms of your life, or only into formal church events?
9:28.action: Invite someone newer in the faith to share a simple meal or errand with you this week, treating them as family.
9:28.prayer: Father, thank You that You welcome us into Your family through Jesus. Help our churches be places where new believers genuinely belong, sharing real life with us and not just watching from a distance. Amen.

9:29.devotion: Saul preached boldly in Jerusalem in the name of the Lord Jesus, engaging Greek-speaking Jews in reasoned discussion, much as Stephen once had. His witness was so direct that his opponents reacted with violence, plotting to kill him. Bold proclamation often stirred strong opposition in the early church.
9:29.reflection: When you speak about Jesus, do you do so with gracious courage or with fearful silence?
9:29.action: Name one conversation this week where you can respectfully share your faith, and prepare a simple, honest explanation of what Jesus means to you.
9:29.prayer: Lord Jesus, give me boldness to speak of You clearly and kindly, even when it is uncomfortable. Guard my words from arrogance, and help me trust You with whatever response my witness receives. Amen.

9:30.devotion: When the believers learned of the plot against Saul's life, they acted wisely. They escorted him to Caesarea and sent him home to Tarsus. Sometimes faithfulness means accepting protection, stepping back from danger, and trusting that God's timing for ministry includes seasons of withdrawal.
9:30.reflection: Can you accept that a season of retreat or safety may be part of God's plan for you, not a failure?
9:30.action: If you are stretched beyond your limits, take one practical step today toward wise rest or boundaries, such as saying no to one demand.
9:30.prayer: Father, You know when to send us forward and when to lead us aside. Teach me to receive protection and rest as gifts from Your hand, trusting that You are preparing work for seasons I cannot yet see. Amen.

9:31.devotion: With the fierce persecution of this period past, the churches across Judea, Galilee, and Samaria enjoyed peace. They were strengthened, walking in reverence for the Lord and in the Spirit's comfort, and they grew. The verse links spiritual health with both holy awe and divine consolation.
9:31.reflection: Is your walk marked by both reverence for God and openness to the comfort of His Spirit?
9:31.action: Set aside fifteen minutes today to pray through one area of your life, asking God to deepen both your reverence and your experience of His comfort.
9:31.prayer: Holy Spirit, comfort Your people, especially those who have known fear and loss. Teach our churches to walk in the fear of the Lord and in Your consolation, so that we may be strengthened and grow. Amen.

9:32.devotion: The narrative turns to Peter, who traveled through the region visiting the saints, the ordinary believers of the church. He came to Lydda, showing that apostolic care extended beyond Jerusalem to smaller communities. Ministry here begins with simply showing up among God's people where they live.
9:32.reflection: Do you think of visiting and checking on fellow believers as real ministry, or only the dramatic moments?
9:32.action: Visit or call one fellow believer today who cannot easily get out, and simply ask how they are doing.
9:32.prayer: Lord, thank You for leaders and friends who show up among ordinary saints. Make me attentive to the believers around me, willing to travel the small distances of visits, calls, and presence that carry Your care. Amen.

9:33.devotion: In Lydda, Peter encountered Aeneas, a man paralyzed and bedridden for eight years. Luke records this condition plainly; Scripture does not attribute his illness to any failure on his part. The scene sets the stage for a display of Jesus' healing power through His apostle.
9:33.reflection: How do you respond to prolonged suffering, in your own life or in others', without easy explanations?
9:33.action: Offer compassionate, practical help today to someone living with chronic illness or disability, without speculation about causes.
9:33.prayer: Lord Jesus, You drew near to those who suffered long. Comfort all who live with paralysis, chronic illness, and disability. Grant them Your presence, provide their practical needs, and teach us to love them patiently. Amen.

9:34.devotion: Peter declared to Aeneas that Jesus the Christ was healing him, commanded him to rise and make his bed, and Aeneas arose at once. The healing belonged to Jesus; Peter was His servant. The command to make his bed pointed Aeneas toward restored, ordinary, responsible life.
9:34.reflection: Where is Jesus inviting you to rise from helplessness and take up ordinary responsibilities again?
9:34.action: Take one small step today toward renewed responsibility in an area where discouragement has left you idle, such as resuming a neglected task or habit.
9:34.prayer: Lord Jesus, You have power to restore what weakness has held down. I trust You with my limitations and my hopes. Raise me up where I have lain down, and send me into ordinary, faithful living. Amen.

9:35.devotion: After Peter healed Aeneas in Lydda, the news spread through the whole region of Sharon. The residents of Lydda and Sharon saw the restored man and turned to the Lord. What began as one act of mercy toward a suffering believer became a doorway of faith for an entire community.
9:35.reflection: When God has helped you, who has noticed and been drawn closer to Him?
9:35.action: Share with one person today how God has helped or provided for you, pointing them toward Him rather than yourself.
9:35.prayer: Lord, thank You for the ways You work in ordinary lives and communities. Use my testimony, however small, to draw others to You. Help me live so that people around me see Your goodness and turn to the Lord. Amen.

9:36.devotion: Tabitha, also called Dorcas, was a disciple in Joppa known for a life of practical compassion. Scripture highlights her good works and charitable deeds—garments she made, care she gave. Her faith was not merely spoken but stitched into everyday service to those in need around her.
9:36.reflection: What tangible act of kindness could become a regular pattern in your life the way Dorcas's sewing was for her?
9:36.action: Identify one person with a practical need this week and do something concrete for them, like providing a meal or needed item.
9:36.prayer: Father, make me a disciple whose faith shows up in deeds, not just words. Open my eyes to the practical needs around me today, and give me willing hands to serve quietly and faithfully, as Tabitha did. Amen.

9:37.devotion: Even a woman full of good works was not spared sickness and death. The believers in Joppa washed her body and laid her in an upper room, grieving their loss. This honest moment reminds us that devoted discipleship does not shield anyone from suffering, and grief is a natural part of love.
9:37.reflection: How do you bring your grief and loss honestly to God and to the community of believers?
9:37.action: Reach out today to someone who is grieving or ill, offering presence and prayer rather than easy answers.
9:37.prayer: Lord, You do not promise Your followers a life free from sickness or loss. When sorrow comes, help me grieve honestly and hold fast to You. Teach me to comfort others with Your presence rather than empty words. Amen.

9:38.devotion: The disciples in Joppa heard that Peter was nearby in Lydda, so they sent two men urging him to come quickly. Their urgency shows how the early church turned to one another—and to God's servants—in crisis. They did not sit helplessly; they reached out in hope.
9:38.reflection: When crisis strikes, do you tend to isolate, or do you reach out to fellow believers for help and prayer?
9:38.action: Tell a trusted Christian friend or pastor about a difficulty you are facing and ask them to pray with you today.
9:38.prayer: Father, thank You for the gift of community. Forgive me for the times I carry burdens alone out of pride or fear. Give me the humility to ask for prayer and help, and make me quick to respond when others call on me. Amen.

9:39.devotion: Peter came to the upper room where the weeping widows surrounded him, holding up the tunics and garments Dorcas had made. Their tears and the clothing in their hands were evidence of her love. A life of quiet service had left marks that grief could not erase.
9:39.reflection: If those you have served gathered around you today, what evidence of your kindness would they hold in their hands?
9:39.action: Begin or continue one ongoing act of service—such as sewing, cooking, or visiting—that meets real needs over time, not just once.
9:39.prayer: Lord, I want my life to leave behind evidence of love like Dorcas did. Show me the people You have placed near me who need steady, practical care. Let my works point to You long after any single act is forgotten. Amen.

9:40.devotion: In the upper room, Peter cleared the space, knelt down, and prayed before speaking to Tabitha's body: "Tabitha, arise." She opened her eyes and sat up. This miracle, like Jesus raising Jairus's daughter, showed that the risen Lord was still working powerfully through His apostles.
9:40.reflection: Do you bring your most hopeless situations to God in prayer before acting, trusting Him with the outcome?
9:40.action: Take five quiet minutes today to kneel and pray specifically about one situation you have considered hopeless, surrendering it to God.
9:40.prayer: Lord Jesus, You are the author of life, and no situation is beyond You. Teach me to pray first, like Peter, before I speak or act. I bring You my impossible situations today and trust You with whatever You choose to do. Amen.

9:41.devotion: Peter took Tabitha by the hand, lifted her up, and called the saints and widows to see her alive. The restoration was shared publicly with the whole grieving community. What God had done was not kept private; the restored woman was returned to the people who loved her and needed her.
9:41.reflection: When God brings restoration in your life, do you share it with others or quietly keep it to yourself?
9:41.action: When you see an answer to prayer or a moment of restoration this week, tell your church family or small group about it.
9:41.prayer: Father, thank You that You restore what we thought was lost, in Your time and way. Help me celebrate Your work openly with my brothers and sisters, giving You the credit. Let shared testimonies strengthen the faith of our whole community. Amen.

9:42.devotion: Word of Tabitha's restoration spread throughout Joppa, and many believed on the Lord. The miracle's greatest fruit was not the event itself but the faith it awakened. God's power, displayed through the church, drew an entire town's attention to Christ rather than to the apostle or the spectacle.
9:42.reflection: Are the stories you tell about God's work pointing people to the Lord, or to people and events?
9:42.action: When you recount God's work in your life this week, deliberately name and credit the Lord rather than people or circumstances.
9:42.prayer: Lord, let everything You do in and through me point people to You. I don't want attention for myself; I want many to believe on You. Use even my ordinary days to make Your name known throughout my community. Amen.

9:43.devotion: After God used Peter to raise Tabitha in Joppa, Peter remained there many days in the home of Simon, a tanner. Tanning was an occupation many considered ceremonially unclean because of contact with dead animals. Peter's willing stay hints at a heart being stretched beyond old boundaries, preparing him for what God would soon reveal.
9:43.reflection: Whose home or company might I be avoiding because of old assumptions rather than God's leading?
9:43.action: Reach out today to someone whose background or circumstances differ from yours, offering a simple act of welcome such as a visit, call, or shared meal.
9:43.prayer: Lord, thank You that Your grace reaches every kind of person, including me. Loosen my grip on old prejudices and make my home and heart places where Your welcoming love can be felt. Amen.

10:1.devotion: The scene shifts to Caesarea, the Roman administrative capital of Judea, where Cornelius served as a centurion in the Italian Regiment. Though a Gentile and an officer of occupying forces, he becomes central to the story of the gospel spreading beyond Israel. God's plan was wider than anyone in the early church imagined.
10:1.reflection: Do I ever assume certain people are outside the reach of God's grace?
10:1.action: Pray by name today for someone you would naturally consider far from God, asking Him to draw that person and give you a humble part in it.
10:1.prayer: Father, You know every person in every place, even those I might overlook or misjudge. Widen my vision to match Your heart, and let the good news of Jesus be shared with all people. Amen.

10:2.devotion: Cornelius is described as devout, a God-fearer whose whole household shared his reverence. He gave generously to the needy and prayed continually. Luke presents a man sincerely seeking God within the limits of what he knew, showing that genuine devotion is never wasted, and God takes notice of those who reach toward Him.
10:2.reflection: Is my devotion to God evident in my generosity and my prayer life, or only in words?
10:2.action: Choose one generous gift today, such as giving to a person in need or a ministry, and pair it with a specific time of prayer.
10:2.prayer: God, make my whole household a place of reverence toward You. Teach me to give freely and pray consistently, not for attention but because I love You and trust You. Amen.

10:3.devotion: At the ninth hour, about three in the afternoon, a customary hour of prayer, Cornelius clearly saw a vision of an angel of God who called him by name. God responded to this seeking Gentile with a direct, personal message. Heaven knew him, and his quiet faithfulness was about to open a remarkable door.
10:3.reflection: Am I attentive to how God might be speaking into my ordinary routines of prayer?
10:3.action: Set aside a specific window today to pray without distraction, then write down anything you sense God may be stirring in you.
10:3.prayer: Lord, You called Cornelius by name, and You know mine. Meet me in my ordinary hours of prayer, sharpen my spiritual attentiveness, and help me respond quickly when You speak. Amen.

10:4.devotion: Startled, Cornelius asked the angel what he wanted. The answer is beautiful: his prayers and alms had come up as a memorial before God. Scripture does not say his good works earned salvation; rather, God remembered and honored his seeking heart. God notices faith expressed in prayer and compassion and responds in His perfect timing.
10:4.reflection: What am I faithfully bringing before God that I may be tempted to think goes unnoticed?
10:4.action: Continue faithfully in one unseen act of devotion today, trusting God sees it even if no person ever does.
10:4.prayer: Father, thank You that nothing offered to You in faith is forgotten. Encourage me in the quiet, hidden places of obedience, and remind me that You see, remember, and care. Amen.

10:5.devotion: The angel's instruction was specific: send men to Joppa for Simon Peter. God often works through ordinary human means, connecting a praying centurion with an apostle. The gospel would come to Cornelius through the appointed messenger and message, showing that God both initiates salvation and provides the people through whom it is shared.
10:5.reflection: Whom has God placed in my life as a link to His truth, and whom might He be asking me to point toward it?
10:5.action: Identify one person who could encourage you spiritually, and reach out to them today; also thank someone who has pointed you toward Christ.
10:5.prayer: Lord, thank You that You work through people to bring people to Yourself. Help me value the messengers You provide and make me faithful to share Your truth with others when You call. Amen.

10:6.devotion: Peter was lodging with Simon the tanner by the sea, a detail linking the two stories and quietly preparing Peter for change. Cornelius was told Peter would tell him what he must do. God's directions were clear and step by step, unfolding faith for both men as obedience would open the way for the gospel to the Gentiles.
10:6.reflection: Am I willing to take the next clear step God gives, even before I see the whole picture?
10:6.action: Name one clear step of obedience God has put before you, and take a concrete action toward it before today ends.
10:6.prayer: Father, thank You that You guide step by step. Give me courage to obey what I already know, trusting You with what I cannot yet see, and prepare me for all You have ahead. Amen.

10:7.devotion: Cornelius obeyed immediately. He chose two trusted household servants and a devout soldier who waited on him continually and sent them to Joppa. His faith showed itself in prompt action, and even his household shared his reverence. The story moves forward because a seeking man did what God said without delay or excuse.
10:7.reflection: When God makes something clear to me, do I act promptly or postpone obedience until it feels convenient?
10:7.action: Complete one act of obedience you have been putting off, such as an apology, a call, a gift, or a commitment, today.
10:7.prayer: Lord, give me the kind of ready obedience Cornelius showed. Deliver me from delay and excuse, and let my household and those around me see faith that acts on Your word. Amen.

10:8.devotion: Cornelius, a God-fearing Roman centurion, had received an angelic instruction to send for Peter. Obediently, he explained everything to his trusted messengers and sent them to Joppa. God was quietly arranging a meeting that would open the gospel's door to the Gentiles, weaving together the obedience of two men who had never met.
10:8.reflection: When God stirs your heart toward something unfamiliar, are you willing to act on it promptly, like Cornelius did?
10:8.action: Identify one nudge from God you have delayed obeying, and take the first concrete step toward it today.
10:8.prayer: Lord, give me Cornelius's readiness to obey. When You whisper direction through Scripture, prayer, or circumstances, help me respond without delay or hesitation. Use my small acts of faithfulness in Your larger plans. In Jesus' name, amen.

10:9.devotion: As Cornelius's messengers approached Joppa, Peter climbed to the rooftop to pray at midday. This was a customary hour of prayer, and the quiet roof offered solitude. Unknowingly, Peter's ordinary rhythm of prayer became the setting for one of the most significant revelations in the early church, showing how God meets us in faithful routines.
10:9.reflection: Do you have a regular time and place for prayer where God can meet you in the ordinary moments of your day?
10:9.action: Set aside fifteen minutes today on your own figurative housetop, a quiet spot, to pray without distractions.
10:9.prayer: Father, thank You for meeting Peter in his ordinary prayer time. Help me build steady rhythms of prayer, trusting that You speak in quiet, faithful moments. Make my routine places into meeting places with You. In Jesus' name, amen.

10:10.devotion: While preparations for a meal were underway, Peter grew hungry and fell into a trance. His physical hunger became the doorway to a spiritual vision. Scripture often shows God using ordinary bodily experiences, like hunger or rest, as moments when His purposes break in, reminding us that our everyday needs and His revelations can share the same hour.
10:10.reflection: How attentive are you to God's presence in the mundane, hungry, ordinary moments of your daily life?
10:10.action: When hunger, fatigue, or routine strikes today, pause briefly and ask God to make that ordinary moment a place of awareness of Him.
10:10.prayer: Lord, meet me in my ordinary hours. Even when my body is hungry or my mind is busy with daily tasks, open my spiritual eyes to what You are showing me. Teach me to expect You in the mundane. Amen.

10:11.devotion: In his trance, Peter saw heaven opened and a great sheet descending, bound at its four corners and lowered to the earth. The vivid image, echoing heaven's direct involvement, signaled that something from God was arriving. Peter's conventional world was about to be gently but decisively unfolded by a vision that came straight from the opened heavens.
10:11.reflection: What assumptions or boundaries in your thinking might God be preparing to stretch or transform?
10:11.action: Write down one belief or assumption you hold about who can receive God's grace, and bring it honestly to God in prayer today.
10:11.prayer: Open my eyes, Lord, as You opened the heavens before Peter. Where my understanding is small or my categories too narrow, enlarge my vision of Your gracious purposes. Help me receive what You are showing me with humility. In Jesus' name, amen.

10:12.devotion: The descending sheet held every kind of creature: four-footed animals, wild beasts, creeping things, and birds. The collection deliberately included animals Jewish law classified as unclean. The picture was comprehensive, nothing left out, foreshadowing the vision's deeper meaning: God's saving purposes would embrace all peoples, not only those Peter naturally considered clean or acceptable.
10:12.reflection: Are there people you quietly categorize as outside God's reach, and how does the completeness of this vision challenge that?
10:12.action: Think of one person or group you tend to keep at a distance, and pray for them by name today, asking God to bless them.
10:12.prayer: Father, Your sheet held everything, leaving nothing out. Forgive me for the people I exclude in my heart. Widen my love until it reflects Your own, embracing even those I find difficult or foreign. Shape my heart like Yours. Amen.

10:13.devotion: A voice came to Peter with a simple command: rise, kill, and eat. To a devout Jew who had faithfully kept the food laws his entire life, the command felt shocking and wrong. God was using Peter's deeply held convictions as the very place to teach a new lesson, preparing him for what the vision truly signified.
10:13.reflection: When God's direction unsettles a long-held conviction of yours, is your first response openness or resistance?
10:13.action: Consider one conviction you hold strongly about faith or practice, and prayerfully ask God to examine it with you today.
10:13.prayer: Lord, like Peter, I sometimes hold my convictions so tightly that I resist Your voice. Give me discernment to know when You are teaching me something new, and courage to listen before I decide. Soften my heart to Your word. Amen.

10:14.devotion: Peter's answer captured a striking tension: "Not so, Lord!" He addressed Jesus as Lord, yet refused the command, citing his lifelong observance of purity laws. His refusal came from sincere devotion, not rebellion. Scripture records his honesty to show that even faithful people can mistake their traditions for God's unchanging will, and need grace to see differently.
10:14.reflection: Is there a place where my sincere religious habits might be standing in the way of obeying what God is actually asking of me?
10:14.action: Name one tradition or habit you practice sincerely, and spend a few minutes prayerfully asking God to show you His heart behind it.
10:14.prayer: Lord, I confess I can say "Not so, Lord" while meaning to be faithful. Forgive me when sincerity blinds me. Help me honor what is good in my traditions while remaining fully open and obedient to You. In Jesus' name, amen.

10:15.devotion: The voice answered Peter a second time with words that reframed everything: what God has cleansed, no one must call common. The lesson went beyond food. As the following verses of the chapter show, God was declaring that Gentiles who turned to Him were cleansed and accepted. Peter must not label as unclean what God Himself had declared holy.
10:15.reflection: Whom have I considered unworthy of God's welcome, and will I let God's verdict on them matter more than my own?
10:15.action: Extend a specific act of welcome today, such as a message, invitation, or kind word, to someone you would normally overlook or avoid.
10:15.prayer: Father, thank You that You cleanse and welcome people by Your grace, not my standards. Tear down the walls of judgment in my heart. Help me to welcome whom You have cleansed, and to see others as You see them. Amen.

10:16.devotion: In Peter's vision, a sheet lowered from heaven held all kinds of animals, and a voice told him to eat. When he refused, citing what was unclean, the voice declared that God had cleansed them. The scene repeating three times underscored its certainty. God was preparing Peter to see people differently, not merely food.
10:16.reflection: What assumptions about other people might God be gently overturning in my own heart?
10:16.action: Notice one group you quietly consider 'outside' God's interest, and pray a sincere blessing for them today.
10:16.prayer: Lord, You see every person as Your creation. Cleanse my heart of judgments I have carried without thinking. Teach me to see others the way You see them, with mercy and welcome. Amen.

10:17.devotion: Peter was still puzzling over the vision when the men sent by Cornelius arrived at his lodging. God often works on two ends at once: preparing the messenger through conviction while already moving the circumstances that will explain it. Peter's confusion became the doorway to obedience.
10:17.reflection: When I don't immediately understand what God is doing, do I stay open long enough to see His purpose unfold?
10:17.action: Hold one unanswered question about your life before God today instead of forcing a quick conclusion.
10:17.prayer: Father, when Your ways puzzle me, keep me patient and attentive. Help me trust that You are arranging things I cannot yet see, and give me grace to wait for Your timing. Amen.

10:18.devotion: The visitors stood at the gate, calling for Simon Peter by name. Unknown to Peter, his address was known to strangers from Caesarea who had traveled seeking him. God's guidance had brought them precisely to the right door, showing how faithfully He coordinates His plans even before we understand them.
10:18.reflection: Where might God already be working in a situation before I have even noticed it?
10:18.action: Thank God in writing today for one time His provision arrived before you recognized your need.
10:18.prayer: Gracious God, You go ahead of me into every circumstance. Thank You for the times Your care reached me before I even knew to ask. Help me live with grateful awareness of Your presence. Amen.

10:19.devotion: As Peter kept reflecting on the vision, the Holy Spirit spoke directly to him, announcing that three men were seeking him. God did not leave Peter to decode the vision alone; the Spirit connected the heavenly picture to the earthly moment, turning contemplation into clear, immediate direction.
10:19.reflection: Am I giving God quiet space to speak into the things I am still thinking through?
10:19.action: Set aside ten unhurried minutes today to bring one confusing matter to God in silence and prayer.
10:19.prayer: Holy Spirit, thank You for guiding me when my own understanding runs out. Speak into my questions, calm my restlessness, and make Your direction clear enough for my next faithful step. Amen.

10:20.devotion: The Spirit told Peter to go with the men, doubting nothing, because God Himself had sent them. Peter's personal scruples about association with Gentiles were not to override God's clear command. Obedience here meant acting on divine instruction even when it crossed familiar religious boundaries.
10:20.reflection: Is there a clear step God is asking of me that my hesitations keep delaying?
10:20.action: Take one obedience step you have postponed—make the call, offer the apology, or extend the invitation today.
10:20.prayer: Lord, forgive me for the ways hesitation masks itself as caution. Give me courage to obey You promptly when You speak, and to trust Your command above my own discomfort. Amen.

10:21.devotion: Peter went down, identified himself honestly, and asked why they had come. His openness set the tone for what followed. Rather than defending himself or retreating, he met the visitors face to face, ready to listen. Humble inquiry often opens the way for God's larger purposes.
10:21.reflection: Do I approach unfamiliar people and situations with honest openness or with guarded self-protection?
10:21.action: Start one conversation today by genuinely asking someone about their situation and listening without interrupting.
10:21.prayer: Father, make me honest and approachable. Remove the defensiveness that keeps me from hearing others, and give me a listening heart that welcomes the people and purposes You bring across my path. Amen.

10:22.devotion: The messengers explained their mission: Cornelius, a God-fearing centurion respected widely for his integrity, had been directed by an angel to summon Peter and hear his words. A devout soldier's earnestness and a heavenly message converged, showing God drawing a sincere seeker toward the good news Peter carried.
10:22.reflection: How might God be using my faithfulness in small, everyday integrity to prepare something far bigger?
10:22.action: Practice integrity in one hidden task today, doing it well even though no one will likely notice.
10:22.prayer: God of Cornelius, You notice those who seek You sincerely and You send messengers to them. Make me faithful in unseen things, ready to carry Your word to whoever You place in my path. Amen.

10:23.devotion: Peter welcomed the messengers in as guests and traveled with them the next day, accompanied by believers from Joppa. His hospitality itself was a first act of obedience to the vision. Crossing the boundary began not with a grand speech but with opening his home and walking alongside them.
10:23.reflection: Whose hospitality or friendship am I withholding because they seem too different from me?
10:23.action: Extend concrete welcome today—share a meal, coffee, or a warm invitation with someone outside your usual circle.
10:23.prayer: Lord Jesus, You welcomed me when I had nothing to offer. Free me from the boundaries I draw around Your love, and make my home and my friendship places of genuine welcome. Amen.

10:24.devotion: Cornelius, a Roman centurion, prepared eagerly for Peter's arrival. He did not keep the good news to himself but gathered relatives and close friends to hear what God would say. His hospitality shows a heart already hungering for God, ready to share the moment with those he loved.
10:24.reflection: Who in your life would you want beside you when God does something significant?
10:24.action: Invite one friend or family member today to join you in church, a Bible reading, or a conversation about faith this week.
10:24.prayer: Lord, give me Cornelius's eager expectancy. Help me not to hoard Your blessings but to gather the people I love so they can also hear from You. Make my home a place of welcome. Amen.

10:25.devotion: When Peter arrived, Cornelius fell at his feet in reverence. Though a man of rank and authority, Cornelius responded to the moment with overwhelming awe. His gesture, while sincere, mistook honor to God's messenger for worship owed to God alone, setting up Peter's gentle correction in the next verse.
10:25.reflection: Have you ever let admiration for a person drift into something closer to worship?
10:25.action: Examine your heart today: thank one spiritual mentor for their influence, and deliberately give God the glory for it.
10:25.prayer: Father, You alone deserve my worship. Thank You for faithful people who point me to You. Keep my gratitude for them from becoming misplaced reverence, and fix my awe on You alone. Amen.

10:26.devotion: Peter refused the honor Cornelius offered, lifting him up and insisting they were both merely human. The apostle who had walked with Jesus modeled humility, deflecting glory from himself. In God's kingdom, no messenger outranks another in worth; all stand equally before the Lord they serve.
10:26.reflection: When someone praises you, can you honestly say, 'I am only a servant too'?
10:26.action: The next time you receive credit, verbally redirect it, thanking God or acknowledging the others who helped.
10:26.prayer: Lord Jesus, keep me from pride when people honor me, and from false humility that seeks praise anyway. Remind me daily that I am simply a fellow human serving the same gracious God. Amen.

10:27.devotion: Peter talked with Cornelius and then entered the house, finding a crowd gathered. This ordinary conversation was itself remarkable, crossing a deep social and religious divide. Peter's willingness to sit and speak with these Gentiles prepared the way for the gospel to reach them fully.
10:27.reflection: Whose company do you avoid that God may be calling you to sit with and listen to?
10:27.action: Start a genuine conversation today with someone from a different background, church, or culture than your own.
10:27.prayer: Father, thank You that the gospel crosses every human dividing line. Give me courage and warmth to converse with people I might naturally keep at a distance, trusting You go before me. Amen.

10:28.devotion: Peter named the barrier openly: long-standing custom warned Jews against entering a Gentile home. But God's vision had taught him not to label any person common or unclean. What God has cleansed, no human tradition may re-condemn. Peter let God's revelation overturn his inherited assumptions.
10:28.reflection: What assumption about certain people might God be asking you to surrender?
10:28.action: Identify one group you quietly avoid or judge, and take one practical step today to treat its members with equal dignity.
10:28.prayer: God of all nations, forgive me for the labels I place on people. You have shown me no one is common or unclean in Your sight. Tear down my inherited prejudices and replace them with Your love. Amen.

10:29.devotion: Because God had spoken, Peter came without objection, though the journey troubled his conventions. Arriving, he humbly asked why he had been sent for, willing to listen before speaking. Obedience opened his mouth, but so did teachability; he did not assume he already understood God's purpose.
10:29.reflection: Do you ask questions before assuming you know what God, or another person, intends?
10:29.action: Before offering advice today, ask one sincere question and listen to the answer without interrupting.
10:29.prayer: Lord, make me obedient when You send me and humble when I arrive. Give me the grace to ask before assuming, and to listen to others as attentively as I want You to listen to me. Amen.

10:30.devotion: Cornelius recounted his devotion: fasting, and prayer at the ninth hour, the traditional time of prayer, when a figure in bright clothing appeared. His story confirms that God notices those who sincerely seek Him, even before they know the full gospel. Piety alone did not save him, but it positioned him to hear.
10:30.reflection: Is there a regular time and place where you consistently meet with God in prayer?
10:30.action: Set a specific daily prayer time today and protect it, even if only ten minutes, for the next seven days.
10:30.prayer: Father, You heard Cornelius when he sought You faithfully. Hear me also as I set apart time to pray. Draw near to my seeking heart, and use my devotion to lead me deeper into Your truth. Amen.

10:31.devotion: The heavenly messenger told Cornelius his prayer had been heard and his alms remembered before God. Generosity and prayer ascended together like a memorial. God is not indifferent to quiet faithfulness; He sees the prayers of the seeking and the gifts given to the needy, and He responds in His timing.
10:31.reflection: What unnoticed act of generosity or prayer of yours might God be remembering right now?
10:31.action: Give quietly today, a gift of money, time, or help, with no announcement, trusting God alone to see and remember it.
10:31.prayer: Gracious God, thank You that You see and remember what others overlook. Accept my prayers and my giving, not as merits I earn with, but as expressions of a heart reaching for You. Respond in Your perfect way. Amen.

10:32.devotion: Cornelius, a Roman centurion, recounts how an angel instructed him to send for Peter, who was staying with Simon the tanner by the sea in Joppa. God was orchestrating a meeting between a Gentile seeker and a Jewish apostle, bridging a cultural divide that seemed uncrossable.
10:32.reflection: Whom might God be asking me to reach across a cultural or social barrier to meet?
10:32.action: Reach out today to someone from a different background than yours with a friendly message, call, or visit.
10:32.prayer: Lord, thank You that You arrange divine appointments across every human divide. Give me courage to respond promptly when You prompt me toward someone unexpected, and make me willing to go wherever You lead. Amen.

10:33.devotion: Cornelius tells Peter that he obeyed the angel's instruction immediately and praises Peter for coming. Then he declares that they are all gathered before God, ready to hear everything God has commanded. His posture models hungry, expectant listening to God's word.
10:33.reflection: Do I come to hear God's word with the same eagerness and readiness Cornelius showed?
10:33.action: Before your next Bible reading, pause and pray, asking God to speak, then listen without rushing.
10:33.prayer: Father, make my heart ready like Cornelius's, gathered before You and eager for every word You command. Remove distraction and dullness, and help me receive Your word with obedience, not merely curiosity. Amen.

10:34.devotion: As Peter begins speaking to Cornelius's household, he voices the lesson God has just taught him through vision and encounter: God shows no partiality. The gospel is not reserved for one people group, nation, or class, but extends to all who come to Him.
10:34.reflection: Do I carry any hidden favoritism that treats some people as less welcome to God than others?
10:34.action: Notice any group you quietly view as outsiders, and pray a genuine blessing over them today.
10:34.prayer: Lord, forgive me for the borders I draw that You never drew. Thank You that Your grace reaches every nation, status, and story. Teach me to see people as You see them, without partiality. Amen.

10:35.devotion: Peter continues: in every nation, whoever fears God and works righteousness is accepted by Him. This is not a declaration that people earn salvation by works, but the opening of God's welcome to all who respond to Him in reverent faith, wherever they come from.
10:35.reflection: Is there anyone I have assumed is beyond God's acceptance before they even had a chance to hear?
10:35.action: Invite someone you have never talked with about faith into an honest, respectful conversation this week.
10:35.prayer: God of every nation, thank You that Your acceptance is not limited by geography, ethnicity, or my assumptions. Widen my heart to match Your welcome, and use me to carry Your invitation to everyone I meet. Amen.

10:36.devotion: Peter proclaims the word God sent to Israel: peace through Jesus Christ, who is Lord of all. The message that began with Israel is now announced to Gentiles, because the peace Jesus brings is not for a select few. His lordship is universal.
10:36.reflection: Where in my life or relationships do I need the peace that Jesus Christ, Lord of all, brings?
10:36.action: Identify one strained relationship, and take one step toward peace today, such as a kind word or apology.
10:36.prayer: Lord Jesus, You are Lord of all, not Lord of some. Thank You for preaching peace into a divided world and into my divided heart. Rule over my conflicts and make me an instrument of Your peace. Amen.

10:37.devotion: Peter reminds his listeners that they already know the word proclaimed throughout Judea, beginning in Galilee after John's baptism. The story of Jesus was not hidden or private; it was public news that had spread through the region, and now its meaning is being made clear to them.
10:37.reflection: Am I letting the well-known story of Jesus become fresh and personally real to me again?
10:37.action: Reread a Gospel account of Jesus's ministry today and note one detail that strikes you anew.
10:37.prayer: Father, I can grow so familiar with the story of Jesus that it loses its wonder. Make the good news fresh to me again, and help me share it naturally, as news worth telling. Amen.

10:38.devotion: Peter describes how God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and power. Jesus went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, because God was with Him. His ministry combined compassionate action and deliverance, showing what life lived in God's presence looks like.
10:38.reflection: Does my daily life leave a trail of doing good the way Jesus's ministry did?
10:38.action: Perform one deliberate act of practical goodness today for someone who is suffering or weighed down.
10:38.prayer: Father, thank You for Jesus, anointed with Your Spirit, who went about doing good. Fill me with that same Spirit so that my ordinary days carry Your kindness to people who are hurting and oppressed. Amen.

10:39.devotion: Peter declares that he and the other apostles are witnesses of everything Jesus did in Judea and Jerusalem, including His death by hanging on a tree. The gospel rests on eyewitness testimony: these men saw His life and His crucifixion, and their message flows from what they actually witnessed.
10:39.reflection: How faithfully am I living as a witness to what I have come to know of Jesus?
10:39.action: Write down briefly how you came to know Jesus, and share that story with one person soon.
10:39.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for witnesses who recorded what they saw so that I could believe. Make my own testimony clear and unashamed, and let my life point others to what You have done. Amen.

10:40.devotion: Peter is speaking in Cornelius's house, telling the gathered Gentiles the heart of the gospel. The Jesus who was crucified did not remain dead: God raised Him on the third day. The resurrection was God's own decisive act, and the risen Jesus was shown openly, not hidden away, so that His victory over death could be witnessed and proclaimed.
10:40.reflection: How does knowing that God raised Jesus from the dead change the way I face my own fears today?
10:40.action: When a worry arises today, pause and say aloud a sentence of thanks that Christ is risen and alive.
10:40.prayer: Risen Lord, thank You that death could not hold You. Help me live today in the light of Your resurrection, with courage and hope in every circumstance. Amen.

10:41.devotion: Peter emphasizes that the risen Jesus appeared not to everyone, but to witnesses God had chosen beforehand, who ate and drank with Him after He rose. These shared meals grounded their testimony in real, bodily experience. Their preaching rests on what they personally saw, touched, and shared with the living Christ.
10:41.reflection: Do I treat the resurrection as real history reported by eyewitnesses, or merely as an idea I find comforting?
10:41.action: Share one reason you believe in the risen Christ with a friend or family member in a natural conversation today.
10:41.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for appearing to Your chosen witnesses and grounding our faith in truth. Strengthen my confidence in the eyewitness testimony of Your resurrection. Amen.

10:42.devotion: Peter explains the commission the risen Christ gave: preach to the people and testify that Jesus is ordained by God as Judge of the living and the dead. The One who was wrongfully condemned by human courts will one day judge all people justly. This authority is the basis for the apostles' bold witness.
10:42.reflection: How does remembering that Jesus is the appointed Judge shape the way I speak about Him to others?
10:42.action: Speak a simple, respectful word of testimony about Jesus to someone today, trusting God with the results.
10:42.prayer: Lord, You have appointed Your Son as Judge of all. Give me courage to testify about Jesus plainly and kindly, and to trust Your perfect justice. Amen.

10:43.devotion: Peter closes his message with the good news the prophets anticipated: through Jesus' name, everyone who believes in Him receives remission of sins. Forgiveness is not earned by background, status, or effort. It comes through faith in Christ, fulfilling what Scripture had promised all along. This welcome is for Jew and Gentile alike.
10:43.reflection: Am I living in the freedom of forgiven sins, or still carrying guilt Christ has already taken away?
10:43.action: Write down a sin you struggle to believe is forgiven, then thank God for remission of sins through Christ's name.
10:43.prayer: Father, thank You that through Jesus' name, whoever believes receives forgiveness of sins. Help me rest in that promise and share it freely with others today. Amen.

10:44.devotion: While Peter was still speaking, the Holy Spirit fell on all who heard the word. God acted even before the sermon finished, confirming that His grace was not waiting on human approval. This moment marks the Spirit's dramatic outpouring on Gentile believers, echoing what happened at Pentecost.
10:44.reflection: Am I open to God working in ways and among people I did not expect?
10:44.action: Listen attentively when God's word is read or preached today, expecting Him to speak to your heart.
10:44.prayer: Holy Spirit, thank You for falling on all who hear the word. Prepare my heart to receive You and to welcome everyone You draw to Yourself. Amen.

10:45.devotion: The Jewish believers who came with Peter were astonished, because the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out on the Gentiles also. Their surprise reveals how deeply ingrained their boundaries were. God's generosity outran their expectations, showing that His gift is given by grace, not restricted by ethnicity or custom.
10:45.reflection: Are there people I quietly assume are outside the reach of God's grace?
10:45.action: Identify one person or group you tend to overlook, and pray for them by name today.
10:45.prayer: Lord, forgive me for the boundaries I draw that You do not. Thank You that Your Spirit is poured out generously. Widen my heart to welcome all whom You welcome. Amen.

10:46.devotion: Peter and his companions heard the new Gentile believers speaking in tongues and magnifying God, the same evidence seen earlier among Jewish believers. Their praise showed that God had genuinely received them. Peter's response follows naturally from what he has witnessed: what God has clearly blessed, no one should deny.
10:46.reflection: When I see God at work in unexpected people, do I rejoice or resist?
10:46.action: Thank God today for one believer whose background or story differs from yours, and tell them you're glad they're part of God's family.
10:46.prayer: Lord, You teach us to magnify Your name in every language and culture. Help me celebrate Your work wherever I see it, without jealousy or doubt. Amen.

10:47.devotion: Peter draws the conclusion no one can argue with: the Gentiles have received the Holy Spirit just as the Jewish believers did, so nothing should prevent them from being baptized with water. The church's boundaries are defined by God's action, not human tradition. Peter commands baptism, welcoming these new believers fully into the family of God.
10:47.reflection: Do I welcome into full fellowship everyone whom God has clearly received?
10:47.action: Reach out warmly to a newer believer in your church this week, perhaps inviting them for coffee or a meal.
10:47.prayer: Father, thank You that You receive all who believe, and that water baptism marks Your welcome. Make our churches places where no one You have received is shut out. Amen.

10:48.devotion: At the climax of Cornelius's household receiving the Holy Spirit, Peter commands these new Gentile believers to be baptized in the name of the Lord. Water baptism publicly marks their full inclusion in God's people. Then the newcomers invite Peter to stay, showing fellowship crossing old boundaries of separation between Jew and Gentile.
10:48.reflection: Who might God be inviting me to welcome as a brother or sister that I have quietly kept at a distance?
10:48.action: Reach out today to someone from a different background in your church or community and share a meal, call, or kind word.
10:48.prayer: Lord, thank You that Your grace reaches every people and nation. Help me welcome those You have received, and celebrate every believer as family in Your name. Amen.

11:1.devotion: Word travels quickly: the apostles and believers in Judea hear that Gentiles have received the word of God. This news is remarkable, even startling, to a community accustomed to thinking of itself in covenantal and ethnic terms. The church now faces how to understand God's surprising work among the nations.
11:1.reflection: When I hear that God is working in unexpected places or among unexpected people, is my first response wonder or suspicion?
11:1.action: Ask God to open your eyes to one way He is working outside your usual circles, and give thanks for it in prayer today.
11:1.prayer: Father, Your word is for all people. Widen my heart to rejoice when You work beyond my expectations, and keep me from narrowing Your grace to my comfort zone. Amen.

11:2.devotion: When Peter returns to Jerusalem, believers of Jewish background who valued circumcision contend with him. Their concern arises from devotion to covenant identity and long-held purity practices, not mere hostility. This moment opens an honest conversation inside the church about what God had done through Peter's experience at Caesarea.
11:2.reflection: When fellow believers challenge me, do I listen for what God may be doing, or do I simply dig into my own position?
11:2.action: If you have an unresolved disagreement with a fellow believer, take one step today toward a gracious, honest conversation.
11:2.prayer: Lord, give me humility when brothers and sisters question me. Where we differ, help us seek Your truth together with patience, listening before speaking, and love before judgment. Amen.

11:3.devotion: The critics press their point directly: Peter entered the home of uncircumcised men and ate with them. In their tradition, table fellowship with Gentiles risked ceremonial defilement. Their objection exposes how deeply cultural and ceremonial habits can shape our sense of who counts as acceptable company before God.
11:3.reflection: What habits or assumptions of mine might be keeping me from sharing fellowship with people God has already accepted?
11:3.action: Identify one social barrier you tend to maintain, and take a simple step across it today, such as sitting with someone new.
11:3.prayer: Father, forgive me for the walls I build that You have torn down. Teach me to see people as You see them, and to share fellowship freely in Christ. Amen.

11:4.devotion: Peter does not respond with anger but explains the whole matter in order from the beginning. He walks the Jerusalem believers through the sequence of events so they can judge for themselves. His patience models how to handle conflict in the church: truthful testimony, given calmly and completely, rather than defensiveness.
11:4.reflection: When my motives or choices are questioned, do I answer with calm, honest explanation, or with irritation and self-protection?
11:4.action: Practice patient explanation today: if someone misunderstands you, respond calmly and tell the whole story without exaggerating.
11:4.prayer: Lord Jesus, You faced misunderstanding without sin. Give me a peaceful spirit to explain myself honestly, to listen well, and to trust You with the outcome. Amen.

11:5.devotion: Peter begins his account in Joppa, where he was praying and fell into a trance. He saw a vision of an object like a great sheet descending from heaven by its four corners. Peter's story starts with prayer and God's initiative, reminding the church that God Himself was directing this new chapter.
11:5.reflection: Am I making space to pray and pay attention to how God may be directing me, especially in areas where I feel settled?
11:5.action: Set aside ten quiet minutes today to pray and ask God to show you any attitudes He wants to reshape in you.
11:5.prayer: Father, You speak and act first, even when I have not asked. Teach me to pray attentively and to recognize Your hand leading me into Your purposes. Amen.

11:6.devotion: Peter looked intently into the vision and considered it carefully. The sheet held four-footed animals, wild beasts, creeping things, and birds of the air, a comprehensive mixture of creatures. Rather than dismissing the strange sight, Peter studied it, showing that receiving God's word often begins with attentive, thoughtful observation.
11:6.reflection: Do I pause long enough to consider carefully what God is showing me, or do I rush past what unsettles me?
11:6.action: When something today surprises or unsettles you, pause and reflect on it in prayer before reacting or forming conclusions.
11:6.prayer: Lord, slow me down. Help me look carefully at what You place before me, to consider it with care, and to respond with a heart that trusts You. Amen.

11:7.devotion: In the vision, a voice tells Peter to rise, kill, and eat. The command confronts Peter's lifelong eating habits formed around the food laws that had marked Israel as distinct. God's voice initiates a change Peter would never have chosen on his own, preparing him to understand that God Himself defines what is clean.
11:7.reflection: Where is God challenging a settled conviction of mine, and am I willing to hear Him before resisting?
11:7.action: Hold one firmly held assumption before God in prayer today, asking Him to purify your convictions by His word.
11:7.prayer: Father, Your voice can unsettle what I have always assumed. Give me ears to hear You, a willing heart, and courage to follow where Your word leads. Amen.

11:8.devotion: Peter is telling the Jerusalem church about his vision. When God invited him to eat animals considered unclean, Peter resisted, using words he had long lived by. His reply mixes loyalty to old boundaries with refusal of God's new direction, showing how deeply habit shapes even a faithful heart.
11:8.reflection: Where might I be saying no to God while calling it devotion?
11:8.action: Identify one assumption you hold about others that may need rethinking, and write it down for prayer today.
11:8.prayer: Lord, You see the boundaries I cling to that You never drew. Give me a humble heart that lets You correct me, and the courage to follow Your voice above my own comfortable certainties. Amen.

11:9.devotion: God's answer to Peter reframes everything: what God has cleansed must not be called common. In context this pointed beyond food to people, preparing Peter to welcome Gentile believers. God declares His purposes, and Peter's role shifts from judging to receiving what God has already made clean.
11:9.reflection: Who has God received that I am still treating as an outsider?
11:9.action: Reach out warmly today to someone you have quietly kept at a distance, perhaps with a message or kind word.
11:9.prayer: Father, thank You that You cleanse by Your grace, not by my standards. Help me never to despise anyone You have received, and to see people as You see them. Amen.

11:10.devotion: Peter notes the vision happened three times before it was taken back to heaven. The repetition shows God's patience with Peter's hesitation. God did not abandon him in his slowness but repeated the lesson until Peter could receive it, then moved events forward immediately.
11:10.reflection: Am I listening long enough for God to finish what He is teaching me?
11:10.action: Return today to something God has been teaching you repeatedly, and spend ten quiet minutes reconsidering it.
11:10.prayer: Patient God, thank You for bearing with my slowness. When I resist Your teaching, do not give up on me. Repeat Your word to my heart until I understand and obey. Amen.

11:11.devotion: Peter connects the timing: right as the vision ended, three men arrived from Caesarea, sent to bring him to Cornelius. The vision and the visitors fit together. God was not merely teaching Peter a lesson about food; He was arranging an encounter that would change the church's understanding of His grace.
11:11.reflection: Do I notice when God's timing brings an opportunity right alongside a lesson?
11:11.action: Pay attention today to unexpected invitations or conversations, and consider whether one may be God's next step for you.
11:11.prayer: Lord, open my eyes to Your timing. When Your lessons and Your opportunities arrive together, give me the wisdom to see Your hand and the willingness to step forward in faith. Amen.

11:12.devotion: The Spirit told Peter to go with the men, doubting nothing, and six believers came along as witnesses. Obedience here meant crossing social boundaries to enter a Gentile's home. Peter did not go alone; the church traveled with him, and shared witness strengthened what God was doing.
11:12.reflection: When God calls me past a comfortable boundary, do I go with confidence or hesitation?
11:12.action: Take one step today toward a person or group outside your usual circle, treating them with genuine respect.
11:12.prayer: Spirit of God, when You call me beyond my comfort, quiet my doubts. Give me companions who encourage faithfulness, and let my obedience open doors for Your work in other lives. Amen.

11:13.devotion: Peter recounts Cornelius's own story: an angel told him to send for Simon Peter. This detail reassured the Jerusalem hearers that the whole chain of events began with God, not Peter's initiative. Both the messenger's vision and Peter's vision were woven into one divine plan of salvation.
11:13.reflection: Can I trust that God may be working in another person's life long before I arrive?
11:13.action: Ask someone today how God has been working in their story, and listen without interrupting.
11:13.prayer: God of all people, thank You that Your grace reaches people long before we do. Teach me to honor Your work in others' lives and to join it humbly rather than assume I own it. Amen.

11:14.devotion: The angel promised words by which Cornelius and his household would be saved. God sent the messenger to a human preacher, showing that salvation comes through hearing the gospel declared. Angels announced and arranged, but God chose Peter's ordinary words as the instrument of His saving grace.
11:14.reflection: Am I willing to speak of Christ, knowing God uses ordinary words to save?
11:14.action: Share one sentence today about what faith in Christ means to you with someone ready to listen.
11:14.prayer: Father, thank You for the good news of salvation through Jesus. Make me faithful and gentle in sharing Your word, trusting that You work through simple, honest words about Christ. Amen.

11:15.devotion: As Peter began preaching, the Holy Spirit fell on the Gentile hearers just as on the apostles at Pentecost. God did not wait for Peter to finish; He confirmed by the Spirit that these people belonged to Him. Peter retells this to show the church that God's welcome cannot be argued with.
11:15.reflection: Do I let God's evident work surprise and reshape my expectations of whom He includes?
11:15.action: Thank God today in prayer for one person or group you once struggled to see as part of His family.
11:15.prayer: Lord, You poured out Your Spirit and widened Your family beyond our expectations. Keep my heart soft to Your grace, ready to rejoice with all whom You receive, and slow to judge. Amen.

11:16.devotion: Peter is defending his visit to Cornelius, a Gentile. He recalls Jesus' promise that His followers would be baptized with the Holy Spirit, not only with water. What happened in Cornelius' house reminded Peter of the Lord's own words, helping him interpret the event rightly.
11:16.reflection: When God works in unexpected ways, do I stop to remember what Jesus has actually said?
11:16.action: Recall one specific promise or teaching of Jesus today, and let it shape how you interpret a current situation.
11:16.prayer: Lord Jesus, when events surprise me, bring Your words to my remembrance. Help me measure what I see by what You have said, and trust Your Spirit at work in places I did not expect. Amen.

11:17.devotion: Peter concludes his defense with humility. If God gave Gentile believers the same gift He gave Jewish believers, Peter could not stand in God's way. He recognized that opposing what God was doing would mean exalting his own traditions over God's gracious initiative.
11:17.reflection: Is there anyone I am subtly withholding from, as though God's grace were not meant for them?
11:17.action: Identify one person or group you tend to overlook, and pray for them by name today.
11:17.prayer: Gracious God, forgive me for the barriers I build that You have torn down. Give me Peter's humility to recognize Your work and never to withstand You. Help me welcome everyone You welcome. Amen.

11:18.devotion: Peter's critics hear his account and fall silent. Instead of arguing further, they glorify God, acknowledging that He has granted repentance and life even to the Gentiles. What began as controversy ends in worship, as their understanding of God's mercy widens.
11:18.reflection: When I am confronted with evidence that changes my thinking, do I respond with worship or defensiveness?
11:18.action: Thank God aloud today for one way His grace has reached people beyond your expectations.
11:18.prayer: Father, grant me a teachable heart like these believers. When You enlarge my understanding of Your mercy, let me respond not with silence of stubbornness but with silence of awe and songs of praise. Amen.

11:19.devotion: After Stephen's death, persecution scattered believers, yet they carried the gospel with them to Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch. At this stage they preached only to Jews. Even tragic circumstances became the means by which the message of Christ traveled outward.
11:19.reflection: When life scatters or uproots me, do I see it as an opening to carry my faith somewhere new?
11:19.action: In one ordinary place you go today, look for a natural moment to mention your faith in Jesus.
11:19.prayer: Lord, You use even hard seasons to spread Your word. Wherever life scatters me, make me a witness. Give me courage to speak of Jesus in the ordinary places my path crosses today. Amen.

11:20.devotion: Among the scattered believers, some men from Cyprus and Cyrene took a bolder step in Antioch: they preached the Lord Jesus to Hellenists, Greeks who had not been part of the usual audience. God blessed their openness, and many believed.
11:20.reflection: Whom might God be calling me to reach that others around me have not thought to reach?
11:20.action: Start a friendly conversation with someone from a different background this week, showing genuine interest and Christlike kindness.
11:20.prayer: Father, thank You for bold believers who crossed boundaries to share Jesus. Give me their spirit, willing to speak to people beyond my usual circle. Use me to carry the good news where it is not yet heard. Amen.

11:21.devotion: As these unnamed believers preached in Antioch, the hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number believed and turned to the Lord. The verse reminds us that fruitful ministry belongs to God's power, not merely human skill or famous names.
11:21.reflection: Am I working in my own strength, or depending on the Lord's hand to rest on what I do?
11:21.action: Before one task today, pause and ask God to work through you, then act trusting His presence.
11:21.prayer: Lord, I need Your hand upon my life and words. Apart from You nothing lasting happens. Work through my simple efforts, and draw people to turn to You. May all fruit be credited to Your power. Amen.

11:22.devotion: News of Gentile conversions reached Jerusalem, and the church sent Barnabas to investigate and shepherd this new work in Antioch. Rather than reacting with suspicion alone, they sent a man known for encouragement, showing pastoral care for a young congregation far away.
11:22.reflection: When I hear of spiritual work outside my circle, do I investigate with curiosity and care rather than quick judgment?
11:22.action: Reach out to a believer in a different church or setting today to express support and encouragement.
11:22.prayer: Father, thank You for churches that care for one another across distance. Make me like Barnabas, ready to see Your grace at work elsewhere and to strengthen others in the faith with genuine encouragement. Amen.

11:23.devotion: When Barnabas arrived in Antioch, he saw clear evidence of God's grace and was glad. He encouraged every believer there to continue with the Lord with purpose of heart. His visit modeled what spiritual leadership looks like: celebrating grace and strengthening perseverance.
11:23.reflection: Do I look for signs of God's grace in others, or only for their faults?
11:23.action: Name one evidence of God's grace in another believer today, and tell that person what you see.
11:23.prayer: Lord, open my eyes to see Your grace in the people around me, so I can rejoice rather than criticize. Make me an encourager who strengthens others to continue with You wholeheartedly and with purpose. Amen.

11:24.devotion: Luke pauses to describe Barnabas, the encourager sent to inspect the new Gentile work in Antioch. His goodness, Spirit-filled character, and evident faith made his ministry fruitful, and many people came to trust the Lord under his influence.
11:24.reflection: Would the people around me describe me as full of the Spirit and faith?
11:24.action: Ask God today to fill you afresh with His Spirit, then speak a word of faith-filled encouragement to one person.
11:24.prayer: Lord, make me like Barnabas—a person of genuine goodness, deep faith, and Your Spirit's presence. Use my life to draw others to You, and let my character reflect Your grace today. In Jesus' name, amen.

11:25.devotion: Facing a growing ministry in Antioch, Barnabas did not try to handle it alone. He traveled to Tarsus to find Saul, the former persecutor now converted, and recruited him for the work God was doing there.
11:25.reflection: Whom could I invite to serve alongside me instead of carrying every burden alone?
11:25.action: Identify one person with gifts you lack and reach out today with an invitation, question, or request to work together.
11:25.prayer: Father, thank You for Barnabas's humility in seeking help. Free me from pride and isolation. Show me the people You want beside me in Your work, and give me courage to invite them. In Jesus' name, amen.

11:26.devotion: Barnabas brought Saul to Antioch, and for a year they taught the church. The believers gathered, learned, and lived so distinctly that outsiders gave them a new name: Christians—people belonging to Christ.
11:26.reflection: Does the way I live actually point others to Christ the way the Antioch believers did?
11:26.action: Commit to one visible act of Christlike love today that an unbelieving coworker, neighbor, or family member might notice.
11:26.prayer: Lord Jesus, You gathered a people in Antioch who were worthy of Your name. Teach me steadily through Your Word, and shape my daily life so that being called a Christian truly describes who I am. Amen.

11:27.devotion: During this season of teaching and growth in Antioch, prophets arrived from Jerusalem. God was speaking to His scattered churches, and the young Gentile congregation was about to receive news that would test its love.
11:27.reflection: Am I listening for God's voice, ready to respond however He directs?
11:27.action: Spend ten quiet minutes today in Scripture and prayer, asking God to make you attentive to His voice and leading.
11:27.prayer: Father, thank You that You speak to Your church. Give me a listening heart, attentive to Your Word and Your Spirit. Prepare me to respond in faith and obedience to whatever You reveal. In Jesus' name, amen.

11:28.devotion: The prophet Agabus, speaking by the Holy Spirit, foretold a severe famine, which history confirms occurred during Claudius's reign. The church in Antioch received this warning not with fear, but as a call to prepare for sacrificial love.
11:28.reflection: How do I typically respond to troubling news—with anxiety, or with trust and readiness to help?
11:28.action: Take one practical step of preparedness this week—setting aside a resource or planning how you could help someone in a crisis.
11:28.prayer: Sovereign Lord, You know the future and warned Your church through Agabus. When unsettling news comes, keep me from panic. Ground me in Your faithfulness, and ready my hands to serve others in hard times. Amen.

11:29.devotion: Hearing of the coming famine, the Antioch disciples resolved to send relief to believers in Judea—people they had never met. Each gave according to his ability, showing that grace produces practical generosity across ethnic and geographic lines.
11:29.reflection: What do I have—time, money, skill—that I could share according to my ability?
11:29.action: Decide today on a specific gift or act of relief for someone in need, and give it according to your actual means.
11:29.prayer: Father, thank You for the generous Spirit in Antioch. Deliver me from hoarding what You have entrusted to me. Teach me to give gladly, according to my ability, for brothers and sisters near and far. In Jesus' name, amen.

11:30.devotion: The church followed through on its resolve, entrusting the gift to Barnabas and Saul, who delivered it to the elders in Judea. Good intentions became completed obedience, carried out through trusted messengers and accountable church leadership.
11:30.reflection: Is there a good intention I have been postponing that God is calling me to actually finish?
11:30.action: Complete one act of generosity or obedience you have planned but not yet done—send the gift, make the call, finish the commitment.
11:30.prayer: Lord, You delight in obedience that follows through. Forgive me for the good intentions I leave unfinished. Give me perseverance to complete what You have prompted, and wisdom to serve Your church faithfully. In Jesus' name, amen.

12:1.devotion: Luke turns to a dark season when Herod Agrippa, seeking political favor, began harassing the Jerusalem church. The young congregation now faced state power turned against it, a reminder that faithfulness to Christ can invite real opposition.
12:1.reflection: When following Jesus costs me something, will I still stand firm?
12:1.action: Pray today by name for persecuted Christians around the world, and ask God to prepare you to remain faithful under pressure.
12:1.prayer: Father, Your church has always faced opposition, yet You have never abandoned Your people. Strengthen believers suffering for Christ's name today. Prepare my own heart to remain faithful, courageous, and prayerful if hardship comes. In Jesus' name, amen.

12:2.devotion: This sobering verse opens the account of persecution in Jerusalem. Herod Agrippa, seeking political favor, executed James, one of Jesus' closest disciples and a leader of the early church. Scripture records James's death plainly, reminding us that following Christ has historically carried real cost for faithful believers.
12:2.reflection: How do I respond when faithfulness to Christ seems costly rather than convenient?
12:2.action: Write a note or prayer today for a Christian you know who is facing hardship, opposition, or persecution for their faith.
12:2.prayer: Lord, thank You for the faithful witness of believers like James who served You at great cost. Strengthen Your persecuted people today, and give me courage to follow You faithfully even when it is hard. In Jesus' name, Amen.

12:3.devotion: Seeing that James's execution pleased some, Herod moved against Peter next, arresting him during the Days of Unleavened Bread, a sacred festival season. Political ambition and public approval drove this persecution. The verse shows how unchecked desire for popularity can lead leaders into grave injustice against innocent people.
12:3.reflection: When have I been tempted to go along with others' approval rather than do what is right?
12:3.action: Identify one situation today where you feel pressure to please people, and choose instead to act with honesty and integrity.
12:3.prayer: Father, forgive me for the times I have valued human approval over faithfulness to You. Guard my heart from the fear of people, and give me boldness to stand for what is right, even when it is unpopular. Amen.

12:4.devotion: Herod imprisoned Peter under extraordinarily heavy guard—four squads of soldiers—planning a public trial after Passover. The elaborate security shows how seriously Herod viewed Peter's influence. Yet this verse sets the stage for God's greater power, as no human security could ultimately frustrate the church's prayers.
12:4.reflection: What seemingly immovable obstacle in my life do I need to entrust to God's power?
12:4.action: Name one difficult situation you have been carrying alone, and deliberately pray about it today instead of trying to fix it only by your own strength.
12:4.prayer: Lord, You are greater than every chain, guard, and locked door in my life. I bring You the situations that feel impossible and ask You to work according to Your will. Help me trust Your timing. In Jesus' name, Amen.

12:5.devotion: While Peter sat in prison, the church did not give up or despair—it prayed constantly and earnestly to God on his behalf. This verse beautifully pairs human helplessness with divine dependence. Facing the loss of their leader, believers turned together to God, whose power exceeds every earthly authority.
12:5.reflection: Is there someone in trouble for whom I could pray with the same persistence the early church showed?
12:5.action: Choose one person in distress and pray for them daily this week, keeping a simple list so your prayers stay consistent.
12:5.prayer: Father, teach me to pray like the early church—constantly, earnestly, and together with others. I lift up those I know who are suffering or afraid. May my prayers be faithful even when answers are not yet visible. Amen.

12:6.devotion: On the very night Herod intended to bring Peter out, Peter was sleeping—bound, guarded, and humanly speaking without hope. His rest reveals remarkable peace, likely trust in God regardless of outcome. The scene sets up a striking contrast between calm faith in a prisoner and the agitation of his persecutors.
12:6.reflection: What would it take for me to rest peacefully in God even in my most anxious circumstances?
12:6.action: Before bed tonight, write down your biggest worry, give it to God in prayer, and choose to leave it with Him as you sleep.
12:6.prayer: Lord, Peter slept peacefully in chains because his rest was in You. I confess my sleepless anxieties and hand them over. Give me that same peace that trusts You fully, whatever tomorrow holds. In Jesus' name, Amen.

12:7.devotion: At the critical moment, God intervened: an angel stood beside Peter, light filled the cell, and the chains fell from his hands. What politics and power had locked down, God opened effortlessly. The verse reminds readers that God's deliverance often arrives at the last moment and in ways we could never arrange.
12:7.reflection: Where in my life do I need to remember that no chain—circumstantial or spiritual—is beyond God's power to break?
12:7.action: Recall one past difficulty where God helped you, and thank Him for it aloud or in a written prayer today.
12:7.prayer: Father, thank You that You are present even in dark places and that Your power is not limited by chains or locked doors. I trust You to work deliverance in Your way and time. Strengthen my faith as I wait. Amen.

12:8.devotion: The angel's instructions were strikingly practical: get dressed, put on sandals, follow me. God's rescue included ordinary, sensible steps.
